discovery-d7d3d348c930d55eef132c86a246e5.title: Halloween Ghost Tours of Lancaster
discovery-d7d3d348c930d55eef132c86a246e5.description: Get in the spirit of the season with spine-tingling tales of haunted mansions, eerie cemeteries and spirits that roam the night! Peer into the shadows and discover the ghosts that roam among us on a candlelight walking tour of downtown Lancaster. Tours run Wednesdays through Sundays in October, and Fridays and Saturdays in November. Purchase tickets in advance at 717-687-6687 or www.ghosttour.com.

discovery-d7d3d348c930d55eef132c86a246e5.price: Not supplied by this calendar; check event details

discovery-4b1b648274ee7364aa4e3c2d534f31.title: Improvised Shakespeare 101 With Renee!
discovery-4b1b648274ee7364aa4e3c2d534f31.description: Discover how to improvise in Shakespeare’s style in this advanced improv class. About the Class: Love. Jealousy. Betrayal. Ambition. Shakespeare used powerful emotions to tell timeless stories that still captivate audiences today–and you can too! Learn the building blocks of improvised Shakespeare including language patterns, narrative devices, and character archetypes to create a larger-than-life Shakespearean comedy on the spot. This class will add techniques to your improv toolkit to use in improvised Shakespeare and beyond. This class requires students to have completed LIP's Improv 201 or Artistic Director approval. Students must be 18 or older for this class. This Class will run Wednesdays from 7pm-9:30pm on the following dates: 10/7, 10/14, 10/21, 10/28, 11/4, 11/11, 11/18, [no class 11/25], and 12/2. This class has a class show on Thursday 12/3 at 7:00pm! Ticket sale close at the end of the day on Sunday 10/4/26. Important: Please check your email the week prior to the start date of your class for any updates. To qualify for the class show you must: Adhere to the Lancaster Improv Players' Code of Conduct. Attend at least six of the eight sessions (ideally all eight). Tickets are on sale until end of day Sunday 10/4!
discovery-4b1b648274ee7364aa4e3c2d534f31.location: Lancaster Improv Players,8 West King Street, Lancaster, PA 17603, USA

discovery-3eb93a0ec8e65226ae20dd2832612b.title: History, Lore & Trivia with Adam Zurn and Benton Webbber
discovery-3eb93a0ec8e65226ae20dd2832612b.description: Join Historic Rock Ford as we welcome Adam Zurn and Benton Webber for a fun afternoon of "History, Lore & Trivia" in the Rock Ford Barn. First, Adam Zurn of Uncharted Lancaster will present "Legendary Tales from the Mighty Susquehanna River." After Adam's presentation, Benton Webber will host his "Revolutionary Lancaster Quiz Bowl." Questions and answers will be in a Quiz Bowl format with teams of four being created. The Rock Ford barn will be set up so that guests will pick a table to sit at upon arrival for Adam's presentation and then those tables of four will become teams for the Quiz Bowl. Meet up with your friends and make a team or join a group at a table and make some new friends! Adam Zurn's presentation will be from 2 PM to 3 PM followed by Benton Webber's Quiz Bowl from 3 PM to 4 PM. This event will be held in the Langmuir Education Room located on the first floor of the Rock Ford Barn. This event is free but registration is required and seating is limited!
discovery-3eb93a0ec8e65226ae20dd2832612b.location: Historic Rock Ford,881 Rockford Road, Lancaster, PA 17602, USA
discovery-3eb93a0ec8e65226ae20dd2832612b.price: Not supplied by this calendar; check event details

discovery-8ff91a1f2e3c900272afb031ea8217.title: Sandeep Das: Raga, Rhythm, & Rasa
discovery-8ff91a1f2e3c900272afb031ea8217.description: Experience the healing power of music with Grammy-winning Tabla maestro and Guggenheim Fellow Sandeep Das. This intimate chamber music concert explores the emotional sentiments of Indian Classical Music known as the Navarasa. Fully relax onstage on a cushion or comfortable chair, or in our spaced-out auditorium seating, as you immerse yourself in the mesmerizing dialogue of exotic instruments, intricate compositions, expressive phrasing, spontaneous improvisations, and joyful folk melodies. Adults $25 | Students $17
discovery-8ff91a1f2e3c900272afb031ea8217.location: Ware Center for the Arts,42 North Prince Street, Lancaster, PA 17603, USA

discovery-4450bebfd8cad7bb830ff6465220dd.title: Ragtime the Musical
discovery-4450bebfd8cad7bb830ff6465220dd.description: A sweeping musical adaptation of E.L. Doctorow’s novel that follows three fictional families in pursuit of the American Dream at the dawn of the 20th Century: Black pianist Coalhouse Walker, Jr. and his beloved Sarah, Jewish immigrant Tateh and his little girl, and a wealthy white family led by matriarch Mother. All grasping for the same dream, if only they can hold on to it.

discovery-065171142d345945d26f8066f82160.title: Improv 101 with Emily!
discovery-065171142d345945d26f8066f82160.description: Your Journey to the Stage Starts Here! About the Class: This is an 8 week long class that will teach the fundamentals of long form Improv Comedy. Topics covered include agreement with a scene partner, character creation, listening as a character and an actor, and exploring the worlds created in scenes. The class ends with a graduation show where the students can show their friends and family the skills learned. Students must be 18 or older for this class! This Class will run Mondays from 7pm-9pm on the following dates: 10/19, 10/26, 11/2, 11/9, 11/16, 11/23, 11/30, and 12/7 . This class has a class show on Saturday 12/12 at 3pm! Important: Please check your email the week prior to the start date of your class for any updates. To qualify for the class show you must: Adhere to the Lancaster Improv Players' Code of Conduct. Attend at least six of the eight sessions (ideally all eight). Attend at least two improv shows during the length of the class. During the class you receive standby tickets for all of our regular shows. These tickets get you into shows for free so long as the show has not soldout! Tickets are on sale until 11:59pm of Friday 10/16!
discovery-065171142d345945d26f8066f82160.location: Lancaster Improv Players,8 West King Street, Lancaster, PA 17603, USA

discovery-c759219131cd09fb694d7f0b784a20.title: Jeffrey Gaines with Special Guest Meaghan Farrell
discovery-c759219131cd09fb694d7f0b784a20.description: Celebrate the best of local music with two acclaimed singer-songwriters who have deep roots in the midstate. Harrisburg native Jeffrey Gaines, revered worldwide for his soul-searching lyrics and powerful live performances, brings his decades-spanning catalog to the stage. Since bursting on the scene with his self-titled 1992 debut album, the charismatic singer-songwriter-guitarist has built a beloved body of recordings that’s won him a large and deeply devoted international fan base and earned him a place on the stage as a supporting act for Tom Petty & The Heartbreakers, Tracy Chapman, and Stevie Nicks with Sheryl Crow, among others. Hailed as "the voice of a generation" by Rolling Stone, Gaines has become one of the most treasured songwriters, vocalists, and inspirations in music today. Harrisburg-born Meaghan Farrell, a singer-songwriter whose compelling voice and dynamic stage presence encourage listeners to “keep it weird,” delivers a vibrant independent sound. A match made for the atrium! Tickets: $25 Presented in partnership with WITF Music, with support from the High Foundation.
discovery-c759219131cd09fb694d7f0b784a20.location: Ware Center for the Arts,42 North Prince Street, Lancaster, PA 17603, USA
discovery-c759219131cd09fb694d7f0b784a20.price: Not supplied by this calendar; check event details

discovery-4657f9d8b0aaf02ad56127cf922f01.title: Improv 101 with Mike!
discovery-4657f9d8b0aaf02ad56127cf922f01.description: Your Journey to the Stage Starts Here! About the Class: This is an 8 week long class that will teach the fundamentals of long form Improv Comedy. Topics covered include agreement with a scene partner, character creation, listening as a character and an actor, and exploring the worlds created in scenes. The class ends with a graduation show where the students can show their friends and family the skills learned. Students must be 18 or older for this class! This Class will run Saturdays from 1pm-3pm on the following dates: 10/24, 10/31, 11/7, 11/14, 11/21, 11/28, 12/5, and 12/12. This class has a class show on Sunday 12/13 at 3pm! Important: Please check your email the week prior to the start date of your class for any updates. To qualify for the class show you must: Adhere to the Lancaster Improv Players' Code of Conduct. Attend at least six of the eight sessions (ideally all eight). Attend at least two improv shows during the length of the class. During the class you receive standby tickets for all of our regular shows. These tickets get you into shows for free so long as the show has not soldout! Ticket sale ends at 11:59pm on Wednesday 10/21!
discovery-4657f9d8b0aaf02ad56127cf922f01.location: Lancaster Improv Players,8 West King Street, Lancaster, PA 17603, USA

discovery-21f93e394dc13d6aab84b989098b45.description: Join us for an evening of great music to support the Shiloh House affordable housing project in Lancaster. The Jordan and Mark Rast Duo will perform at Redeemer Lutheran Church on Nov 6 at 7pm to raise money for this important project. Free admission with donations accepted for the Shiloh House project. Refreshments to follow concert. Jordan and Mark Rast Duo Jordan and Mark are a father/son duo with a shared love for bluegrass and old-time music —both old and contemporary. They perform on multiple instruments (fiddle, banjo, guitar, mandolin, resonator guitar) and include both originals and standards in their repertoire. You will hear a variety of instrumental and vocal music when you see them, all of it performed with joy! Jordan is an accomplished songwriter and has performed solos as well as many configurations with others over the years. Mark has been a long term member of local Bluegrass bands Colebrook Road and Vinegar Creek Constituency. Shiloh House Project The Shiloh House project is a partnership project between Redeemer Lutheran Church and Chestnut Housing, an affordable housing organization in Lancaster. It will involve creating two affordable housing units in the former church parsonage at Redeemer. With the support of our friends, neighbors, and community, we will raise the funds needed to complete this important project.

discovery-2b9ba1569900a0603e1176fdaef451.title: Heartland Marimba Festival – FREE
discovery-2b9ba1569900a0603e1176fdaef451.description: Make the Ware Center part of your Lancaster First Friday route! 7 pm • Lobby Uncover the fascinating history and science behind the marimba with members of Heartland Marimba. This special presentation explores how the instrument produces its distinctive sound, traces its journey from Africa through Central America to the classical music stage, and reveals the surprising Pennsylvania connections behind its history. Discover how U.S. companies and performers helped introduce the marimba to classical music, and hear the untold stories of the musicians who shaped the instrument’s legacy. Among them is Clair Musser, widely regarded as the “godfather” of the classical marimba, who was born in Manheim, Pennsylvania. The story continues in Lancaster, where Reg Kehoe performed across the country for nearly 20 years with the Marimba Queens, a popular all-female marimba ensemble based in Lancaster from the 1930s through the 1950s. Whether you are a longtime marimba enthusiast or simply curious about this remarkable percussion instrument, join Heartland Marimba for an engaging look at marimba history, music, acoustics, and its unique Pennsylvania roots. Admission: FREE and open to the public! Accessibility: There will be a pre-show touch tour for blind and low-vision patrons. Please get in touch with Barry Kornhauser to learn more.

discovery-31f45cd0f6f9645c0f81d680ba46fd.title: "Persuasion" - A One Act Play Inspired by Jane Austen
discovery-31f45cd0f6f9645c0f81d680ba46fd.description: “Persuasion” will be performed within the rooms on the first floor of the circa 1794 General Hand Mansion on November 6, 7, 13, 14, and 21 at 7:00 PM and 8:30 PM and November 22 at 2 PM and 3:30 PM. “Persuasion” relates the story of Anne Elliot, an aristocratic young lady who declines marrying Captain Frederick Wentworth at a youthful age even though she deeply loves him. After a period of seven years, Anne and Wentworth meet again and must resolve their feelings through a series of encounters that are highlighted in the play. This one-act play, inspired by scenes from Jane Austen’s novel, was adapted for Historic Rock Ford by Samuel Slaymaker. Due to space constraints within the rooms of the Hand Mansion, audiences are limited to 15 guests per performance. Guests are standing for the entire performance and will be moving from room to room following the action of the play. Tickets must be purchased in advance. Due to space limitations for each performance, tickets are not available at the door.

discovery-68bb3e4551f68e3a502893397f343a.title: The Foolbright Scholars' Play Lab with Angie Foster
discovery-68bb3e4551f68e3a502893397f343a.description: How can we liberate ourselves from the "shoulds" and "should nots" that can constrain our natural capacity to be authentic, playful and creative? We'll explore through movement, games, and improvisation, and use the clown's ability to take risks and put logic aside to make way for the imagination. What is important is not "getting it right" but rather finding the magic of being surprised by what reveals itself when all else falls away. No experience required, only a willingness to play. We encourage the beginner-est of beginners! For more information and to register: actsofjennius.com/event-list
discovery-68bb3e4551f68e3a502893397f343a.location: Tenfold,308 East King Street, Lancaster, PA 17602, USA

discovery-95d0eeb2cc9ef204f910e912fb254a.title: African American Heritage Walking Tour Downtown Lancaster
discovery-95d0eeb2cc9ef204f910e912fb254a.description: This tour is focused on the Underground Railroad and includes four authenticated Underground Railroad sites. Because the Underground Railroad was by necessity secret, uncovering the details of its existence has required a great deal of detective work. This tour includes the latest research and recent discoveries which further reveal the rich fabric of African American history in Lancaster before and after the Civil War.

discovery-edca2602cc4ddb77cb8d25d0609809.title: African American Heritage Walking Tour of Historic Southeast Lancaster
discovery-edca2602cc4ddb77cb8d25d0609809.description: The Southeast Area tour highlights that liberation is up to African Americans, whose experiences represent a complex connection to their past—both the trauma of enslavement and the resilience of their heritage. This tour brings to life the triumph of the African American community as it built a culture of service, faith, and social activism, alongside the tragedy of Urban Renewal, which saw the demolition of 14 square blocks of thriving businesses, churches, and civic associations. The fabric of the community was ruptured as individual homes were replaced with public housing and vibrant community spaces were obliterated. This tour also traces the life stream and economic castration of that community, which was attacked by the policy of Urban Renewal, but which has not been forgotten or erased.
discovery-edca2602cc4ddb77cb8d25d0609809.location: Crispus Attucks Community Center, 407 Howard Avenue, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States

discovery-678a97a73e88d987b84b48a4da2dd3.title: Disposable Humanity
discovery-678a97a73e88d987b84b48a4da2dd3.description: Join us at the Ware Center for a free screening of the film Disposable Humanity—plus a community discussion panel and a Q&A with the filmmakers. The Mitchell family—esteemed Disability Studies scholars and filmmakers—delve into the chilling legacy of the Nazi Aktion T4 program. This investigative documentary recounts the long-obscured history of how over 300,000 disabled individuals became the initial victims of the Third Reich. Targeted by the T4 program as having a “life unworthy of living,” their murders laid the groundwork for the Holocaust that followed. 6:15 PM • Pre-show community panel discussion Post-show • Q&A with director Cameron S. Mitchell Co-presented by the MU Disability Film Festival and Congregation Shaarai Shomayim.
discovery-678a97a73e88d987b84b48a4da2dd3.location: Ware Center for the Arts,42 North Prince Street, Lancaster, PA 17603, USA

discovery-29549f2bca2c8bb482a45f297e6bf7.description: Community Preview Nights include a pre-show reception and an opportunity to connect with Lancaster vendors, businesses, and organizations. Based on the popular comic strip by Harold Gray, Annie has become a worldwide phenomenon and was the winner of seven Tony Awards, including Best Musical. The beloved book and score by Tony Award winners, Thomas Meehan, Charles Strouse and Martin Charnin, features some of the greatest musical theatre hits ever written, including “Tomorrow.”

discovery-82639f4a2575b37d1af68cfb299db4.title: ExtraGive Junior
discovery-82639f4a2575b37d1af68cfb299db4.description: Friday, November 20, 2026 • 5-8 pm • Lobby Why should adults have all the fun during the ExtraGive? Help us celebrate the Lancaster County Community Foundation’s annual Extraordinary Give with a fun event designed for kids of all ages! Our young guests will experience a variety of free entertainment and creative table activities developed just for them by community benefit organizations, including: • Church World Service • Imani Edu-tainers • Lancaster Shakespeare Theatre • Lone Oak Animal Assisted Therapeutic Services • Music for Everyone • New School Montessori • Pennsylvania Dutch Council, Scouting America • SWAN • Touchstone Foundation …and more! Plus, a puppetry workshop from the performers of Grand Pistachio (including a sneak peek at their show Layer the Walls) at 6:30 pm! Immerse your kids in the joy of giving back! This is a free event, and all are welcome.

discovery-50fc69fd9badac2b31b5f23c3b6040.title: From Solitude to Triumph with Lancaster Symphony Orchestra
discovery-50fc69fd9badac2b31b5f23c3b6040.description: Experience a powerful emotional journey as the Lancaster Symphony Orchestra presents three deeply lyrical masterworks. Copland's Quiet City evokes urban solitude and contemplation, while Barber's Violin Concerto—performed by Sphinx Competition winner Amaryn Olmeda—offers pensive, elegant songfulness that moves from introspection to brilliant virtuosity. The concert culminates with Sibelius' triumphant Symphony No. 2, building from reflection to a glorious, uplifting finale. From quiet contemplation to radiant celebration, this program reveals the full range of the human spirit through three profoundly beautiful works. Showtimes: November 20th @ 7:30 PM November 21st @ 2:30 PM & 7:30 PM November 22nd @ 2:30 PM

discovery-4973630e93ea820ca3ef70be12e201.title: Illumination
discovery-4973630e93ea820ca3ef70be12e201.description: Step into the glow, where candlelight, harmony, and the beauty of the holiday season surround you. This intimate experience returns newly imagined — beloved songs reborn in-the-round by radiant performers and rich live music. Every seat is wrapped in warmth and wonder, offering moments of peace and a welcome rise of joy in the midst of the season’s rush. Immerse yourself in this soul-stirring concert that reminds us of what still feels sacred and leaves you carrying a little more light with you. The beloved book and score by Tony Award winners, Thomas Meehan, Charles Strouse and Martin Charnin, features some of the greatest musical theatre hits ever written, including “Tomorrow.”

discovery-043e794cd07ad51b0a5de9d4cad85c.title: Layer The Walls: Turn of the Century
discovery-043e794cd07ad51b0a5de9d4cad85c.description: Saturday, November 21, 2026 • 3 PM • Steinman Hall In one Lower East Side tenement, forty layers of wallpaper were found clinging to the walls, each piece applied by a new immigrant family. Using puppetry, masks, and live action, Layer the Walls tells the incredible stories held within each layer—an Irish immigrant helping to build the Brooklyn Bridge, Italian brothers surviving the Great Blizzard of 1888, and two Russian Jewish garment workers joining the Uprising of 20,000 to fight for safety. Recommended for ages 8 and up. 2 PM • Lobby • Free kids’ activities and crafts! Tickets: Adults $15 • Students: $10 Accessibility: ASL interpretation, sensory-friendly accommodations, and audio description will be available. There will be a pre-show touch tour for blind and low-vision patrons. Please get in touch with Barry Kornhauser to learn more.

discovery-54b01842c752b29208562dc1b5392c.title: Annie Accessibility Performance
discovery-54b01842c752b29208562dc1b5392c.description: ASL Interpretation: Certified interpreters for select performances provide American Sign Language interpretation. To access special reserved seating, complete an Accessibility Ticket Reservation Form. If you need to cancel your reservation, contact access@thefulton.org so that we may extend an offer to wait-listed patrons. The Pay-What-You-Want program is available for patrons who are deaf or hard of hearing at all ASL interpreted performances. Audio Description is a carefully timed narration of the onstage visual elements in the performance, including the action, costumes, and scenery. Program notes via headset are available 10 to 15 minutes before show time, and a touch tour may be available 1 hour before the show depending on the production (details will be sent via e-mail if a touch tour is available and a separate no-cost reservation will be required). The simultaneous description is broadcast live via an inconspicuous FM receiver. Patrons may choose a single earpiece, dual headset, or a neck loop (for patrons using a hearing aid with a “T” switch), and the device may be used in any seat in the theatre. Patrons may pick up their receiver and headset, free-of-charge, at Audience Services, located in the coat room on the right side of the main lobby. Open-Captioned performances provide patrons with live text presentation of onstage dialogue on a LED screen situated in a box to the right side of the stage. The captions seen on the LED screen may be read from most seats in the theatre, though many prefer seats in the Parquet or Orchestra sections for the best view. An experienced captioner scrolls text in sync with the actors’ spoken word. Tickets can be reserved at the box office or online. The Pay-What-You-Want program is available for patrons who are deaf or hard of hearing at the open captioned performances listed below. Please fill out the Accessibility Ticket Reservation Form for the Pay-What-You-Want rate for the performances listed below. Based on the popular comic strip by Harold Gray, Annie has become a worldwide phenomenon and was the winner of seven Tony Awards, including Best Musical. The beloved book and score by Tony Award winners, Thomas Meehan, Charles Strouse and Martin Charnin, features some of the greatest musical theatre hits ever written, including “Tomorrow.”

discovery-3221a385a3212cd3b741ee6d407b02.title: Yuletide at Historic Rock Ford
discovery-3221a385a3212cd3b741ee6d407b02.description: Celebrate the Yuletide season in 1790s style as the Hand Mansion is adorned in festive holiday finery. Enjoy a visit filled with: Guides in the Mansion's rooms relating various aspects of the Yuletide season during the Hand family's residency at Rock Ford Dance demonstrations reminiscent of late 18th and early 19th century celebrations Live traditional music to set the Yuletide mood Open hearth cooking that brings the past to life In addition: The first floor of the Rock Ford Barn will be open to our Yuletide guests: Warm up with concessions such as hot chocolate Listen to live Early American Music by Forbes Road Frolic Enjoy a creative children's activity Relax around fire pits in the area in front of the Barn (weather permitting) For your convenience, restrooms will be available in the Barn Your timed entry ticket is for the Hand Mansion. Timed entries help spread out the crowd inside the Mansion. Guests explore the Mansion at their own pace with an average visit lasting about 60–75 minutes. Activities in the Hand Mansion and the Barn close promptly at 8 PM. If your timed entry ticket for the Hand Mansion is closer to 8 PM, please plan accordingly to include time to visit the Barn. Please note that the Snyder Gallery is not open during this event. Adults: $20 Senior: $18 Youth (6-17): $10

discovery-d9646085e32ef0bce7851747818d27.title: Tales & Legends with the Lancaster Symphony Orchestra
discovery-d9646085e32ef0bce7851747818d27.description: Music's greatest storytellers take center stage in a program dedicated to the art of musical narrative. Wagner's grand Prelude to Die Meistersinger opens with themes of mastery and tradition, followed by the world premiere of Austin Wintory's Interactive Concerto for Guitar featuring 4-time Grammy-nominated guitarist Mak Grgić in an innovative new work that bridges classical and contemporary worlds. The concert concludes with Rimsky-Korsakov's enchanting Scheherazade—the ultimate musical storyteller—spinning tales from the Arabian Nights with exotic melodies, shimmering orchestration, and the seductive voice of the solo violin. From European legends to interactive innovation to Arabian tales, this concert celebrates music's timeless power to tell extraordinary stories.

discovery-6518da14b8ca71a520111d330c79d9.title: Lancaster City Fall Art Walk
discovery-6518da14b8ca71a520111d330c79d9.description: Explore Lancaster City Art Walk & Hunt for Art! Please Note: A small number of ArtWalk locations are operating on a different schedule. Businesses that have abbreviated hours or Sunday closure are indicated on the map. This year’s Lancaster City Fall Art Walk has a new way to explore the city’s galleries, pop-ups, and creative spaces: a self-guided Art Walk Scavenger Hunt! Pick up your Art Walk map and scavenger hunt sheet at most participating galleries and pop-up locations, then hit the streets and start exploring. Each participating location has a clue tied to artwork on display, with one clue for each numbered location on the map. How to enter: • Collect answers to the clues as you make your way around Art Walk • Get at least 20 answers correct • Drop your completed sheet in one of the designated drop boxes at the galleries indicated on the map • One winner will receive a $250 voucher toward a purchase of $250 or more at any LCAC member gallery Mark your calendars for one of our favorite events of the season! Take a stroll through the city and explore your favorite galleries, museums, and pop – up artist locations. Enjoy live demonstrations from talented local and regional artists, along with a variety of fun and festive events for all ages. It’s the perfect time to start finding that special something for your special someone – just in time as we head into the holiday season!

discovery-c1cd5d999baaaedf3167c70264d1bb.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour
discovery-c1cd5d999baaaedf3167c70264d1bb.description: Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally! Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century. Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI. But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region. As you explore, you’ll stop at five handpicked local spots to enjoy a curated tasting menu featuring hearty breakfast sandwiches, fresh fruits, sweet pastries, and other morning favorites. Please note: This tour offers vegetarian-friendly options only. If you have other dietary needs, we recommend our International Food Tour for a better fit. Whether you’re passionate about history, love discovering new flavors, or just want a memorable way to see the city, the Lancaster History & Breakfast Tour is a great choice for solo explorers, couples, and groups alike.

Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century. Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI. But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region. As you explore, you’ll stop at five handpicked local spots to enjoy a curated tasting menu featuring hearty breakfast sandwiches, fresh fruits, sweet pastries, and other morning favorites. Please note: This tour offers vegetarian-friendly options only. If you have other dietary needs, we recommend our International Food Tour for a better fit. Whether you’re passionate about history, love discovering new flavors, or just want a memorable way to see the city, the Lancaster History & Breakfast Tour is a great choice for solo explorers, couples, and groups alike.

Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century. Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI. But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region. As you explore, you’ll stop at five handpicked local spots to enjoy a curated tasting menu featuring hearty breakfast sandwiches, fresh fruits, sweet pastries, and other morning favorites. Please note: This tour offers vegetarian-friendly options only. If you have other dietary needs, we recommend our International Food Tour for a better fit. Whether you’re passionate about history, love discovering new flavors, or just want a memorable way to see the city, the Lancaster History & Breakfast Tour is a great choice for solo explorers, couples, and groups alike.

discovery-1ac9294231fcbb0472620462ae6a75.title: Ephrata Shadows
discovery-1ac9294231fcbb0472620462ae6a75.description: Downtown Ephrata has a few stories it has never quite finished telling. Join Mainspring of Ephrata, and the Historical Society of the Cocalico Valley, for Ephrata Shadows – a guided historical ghost tour through our downtown streets, where cloaked guides share spine-tingling tales of local legends, unexplained phenomena, and the restless spirits said to still roam the area. Along the way, your guides will share the historical facts about our buildings and the stories behind the folklore. It’s a walking tour for ages 16 and up that blends real history with the ghost stories passed down through generations – and you’ll come away knowing downtown Ephrata a little better, and maybe looking over your shoulder a little more. Two Tours to Choose from, each last about an hour and has two departures (6:30 and 8:00 PM): West End – departs from the Historical Society of the Cocalico Valley, 237-249 W. Main St., Ephrata East End – departs from Hampton Inn & Suites, Ephrata Mountain Springs, 380 E. Main St., Ephrata NEW THIS YEAR – GHOST HUNT EPHRATAA real paranormal investigation experience conducted by our friends at the Paranormal Nut Podcast. Join them on site and see what turns up. Locations to be announced — watch this event for details and tickets. NOTE: This is an add-on experience that runs from 9:30-11:00 PM. PRO TIPS This is an outdoor walking tour. Wear comfortable shoes. The route includes some inclines, so please come prepared. East End tours start at the Hampton Inn, head down the hill along E. Main St. and finish back at the top of the hill at the Hampton Inn. West End tours start and end at the Historical Society. Rain or shine – please dress for the weather. Costumes? Please leave them at home. Our guides will be in black cloaks, and we’d like them easy to spot. The walking tour is a family friendly event, please use your digression for the walking tour. The Ghost Hunt is limited to ages 16 and up. Tickets: Tickets on Sale! Walking Tour Tickets $15 each Ghost Hunt tickets are $25 each. Note this is an add-on event. The tour is not included with the Ghost Hunt ticket. A limited number of tickets are available for guests without online access. Call Mainspring of Ephrata at (717) 721-6196 to reserve.Note: Groups are small and tickets are limited so that we can ensure a great experience for all of our guests.

discovery-6d5c73fb5c6482534dae161cb46761.title: Live Music with Mitch Gregory at Cherry Crest Adventure Farm
discovery-6d5c73fb5c6482534dae161cb46761.description: Check out our amazing lineup of musicians that will be performing live right here at the farm! Join us on select Friday evenings and Saturdays for toe-tapping tunes from our favorite bands. Mitch is a multi-instrumentalist playing guitar, slide guitar, the Wazinator, and is an accomplished harmonica player, and vocalist. Since the 80’s Mitch has performed through out Pennsylvania – Jazz, Blues and Rock collaborations in 2019, Mitch began entertaining as a solo performer. Mitch embarked on an eighteen month residency at the Boomerang/Harrisburg Comedy Zone focused on the blues and assembling material for his current project MITCH GREGORY BLUES. Mitch is performing Texas blues, New Orleans blues, Chicago blues, British and country blues in the styles of: Stevie Ray Vaughan, ZZ Top, BB King, Dr. John, Stray Cats, Rolling Stones, The music of Louis Jordan and much more. discovery-b90d981642b3d2e7b5360e3173d5a2.title: Live Music with Songsmith at Cherry Crest Adventure Farm
discovery-b90d981642b3d2e7b5360e3173d5a2.description: Check out our amazing lineup up of musicians that will be performing live right here at the farm! Join us on select Friday evenings and Saturdays for toe-tapping tunes from our favorite bands. Songsmith is the creative collaboration of experienced musicians Steve Davis and Lynn Royer. Bringing talent, experience, and creativity to every performance, Songsmith is a breath of fresh air to the Central PA acoustic music scene. Playing an eclectic mix of covers, arrangements, and originals, Songsmith brings fun, quality entertainment and industry professionalism to your venue or event. Lynn Royer: Vocals & Hand Percussion Lynn has provided exceptional vocal abilities to a number of musical projects- both acoustic and electric and she has a beautiful tonal quality- both accurate and emotive. Her song writing skills are first-rate, with several songwriting awards to her credit. Lynn is also a teacher for children with special needs. Steve Davis: Guitar & Vocals Steve is a powerful acoustic and electric guitarist employing tasteful use of live loop and other technologies (never prerecorded) he has the ability to play in a wide range of styles. Steve also adds lead and harmony vocals to the mix. Additional Fun Things To Do in Lancaster? discovery-67be8fb743cac453996192a58b7f1c.title: Stephen Schwartz: A Benefit Concert for Prima
discovery-67be8fb743cac453996192a58b7f1c.description: 📍 Rock Lititz – 100 Rock Lititz Blvd, Lititz, PA Broadway legend Stephen Schwartz — the Grammy, Oscar, and Tony Award–winning composer of Wicked, Pippin, Godspell, Pocahontas, The Hunchback of Notre Dame, The Prince of Egypt, and Enchanted — comes to Lancaster County for a once-in-a-lifetime benefit event at Rock Lititz. At the piano, Schwartz will perform his most beloved works and share stories from a career that has shaped Broadway and Disney alike. He is joined by powerhouse Prima performers, filling the space with music, heart, and meaning. But this evening is about more than a concert. It’s a moment to fuel the next great cultural movement in Lancaster. Just as Rock Lititz redefined what’s possible in live music, Prima is redefining what’s possible in live theatre — making Lancaster the launchpad for bold, original works that premiere locally before reaching national stages. Your participation helps fuel cultural vitality, community vibrancy, and economic growth for our region. WHY THIS NIGHT MATTERS Rock Lititz showed that the world’s biggest tours can start here. Prima is proving that tomorrow’s great theatrical works can, too. This benefit event fuels Prima’s mission to invigorate lives through fresh theatrical experiences — performances that are intimate, joyful, and deeply human. Your support helps: Launch bold new theatrical works born in Lancaster. Bring national artists and creative voices to our community. Give audiences world-class experiences first, right here at home. This night ensures Lancaster isn’t just consuming culture — it’s creating it. discovery-664deb929e9a98dc4d47f5eace44da.description: Celebrate the season with a joyful, high-energy holiday spectacular bursting with music, nostalgia, and breathtaking wonder! Journey into Toyland, where imagination comes alive in vibrant, whimsical style—and even Santa and Mrs. Claus get in on the fun. Enjoy audience-favorite hits from White Christmas, then travel back in time as we recreate a 1940s holiday radio show complete with a heartfelt military tribute and classics like “I’ll Be Home for Christmas.” Feel the excitement soar with a spellbinding aerial performance set to the powerful sounds of Trans-Siberian Orchestra, and wrap it all up with a dazzling finale that fills the theater with the warmth and spirit of the holidays. Perfect for guests of every age, this magical Christmas experience is sure to make your season shine. discovery-1d22887630f338f341c9c92844a7f0.title: Little Explorer and Me at North Museum
discovery-1d22887630f338f341c9c92844a7f0.description: Sign up for an exciting, hands-on program where curiosity and learning come to life as Little Explorers and their grown ups experiment and discover together. Where curiosity and learning come to life as Little Explorers and their grown ups experiment and discover together. Every month, a trained facilitator guides you through a new theme that sparks your child’s imagination while helping build critical skills through fun and interactive play. Each activity is designed to be easy for you to recreate at home with everyday materials, giving your child the chance to explore and engage with the world around them. Whether it’s learning about the wonders of sound, exploring the colors of the rainbow, or discovering the magic of play, your child will gain valuable knowledge they can use in everyday life. PRE-REGISTER—We kindly ask that all register in advance of attending this program so our facilitator can prepare materials. Registrations do not grant access to the museum. All non-members must purchase a general admission ticket ($13 each) online or at the door. BUY TICKETS–GENERAL ADMISSION Members enter FREE. Wednesdays at 10:00 am & 3:00 pm COME FOR LITTLE EXPLORER AND ME, STAY FOR THE PLANETARIUM SHOW 11am—One World, One Sky, Big Bird’s Adventure.

discovery-f36a914c644152ff0a9819e62d1e33.title: The Christmas Rush at Bird-in-Hand Stage
discovery-f36a914c644152ff0a9819e62d1e33.description: Attention shoppers—and showgoers! On the day before Christmas, the biggest department store in a small American town has announced a Last-Minute Madness Sale. Will the harried staff be able to handle the onslaught? Will the Santa in the lobby raise enough to save the town’s soup kitchen? And will the recently widowed Alice and her daughter find what they are so desperately seeking? This brand-new show from Blue Gate Musicals is big on laughs, full of heart and has a score that sounds like it stepped right off the Broadway stage. Give yourself a gift and make sure to see The Christmas Rush! All she needed was 3 more hours, 2 more gifts and 1 small miracle!

discovery-96f76f849b6586099aa5d3a1e4e38a.description: November 3 – December 30, 2026 Coupon Step into a storybook journey that whisks you from a charming Bavarian mountain village to the bustling merriment of Santa’s North Pole. Dazzling costumes, glistening gowns, and enchanting sets bring every magical moment to life – so vividly, you’ll feel as though you’ve stepped straight into the pages of a holiday classic. It’s a heartwarming theatrical celebration of Christmas – rich with nostalgia, sparkle, and pure holiday delight. There are many other Christmas events taking place in Lancaster County throughout the Christmas holiday season. See our Christmas in Lancaster page to learn more. discovery-8f6df156331e7ff171b90eb26548d1.title: Live Music with Greg Grasa at Cherry Crest Adventure Farm
discovery-8f6df156331e7ff171b90eb26548d1.description: Check out our amazing line up of musicians that will be performing live right here at the farm! Join us select Friday evenings and Saturdays for toe tapping tunes from our favorite bands. A couple of Taylor acoustic guitars and a crowd-pleasing repertoire that spans the musical genres of rock, folk, country, soul and the blues. It’s an entertaining combination that has kept Greg Grasa in constant demand at taverns, restaurants, festivals, civic functions and private engagements throughout central Pennsylvania for more than 30 years. Through three decades on stage, Greg has never lost his passion for playing and singing the music he loves. Whether it’s a gig at a local bar for a handful of patrons, or for a festival crowd of hundreds, he delivers the same energized show that engages the audience and has them singin’ along to an eclectic blend of familiar covers from the ‘60s, ‘70s, ‘80s and ‘90s, as well as some Grasa originals. discovery-c33e1b1907f34423b62bcc86261fc8.title: Pumpkin Madness Festival – Cherry-Crest Adventure Farm
discovery-c33e1b1907f34423b62bcc86261fc8.description: How many ways you can bid farewell to a pumpkin? Join us as we embark on a thrilling quest to discover the ultimate pumpkin destruction techniques. From smashing and throwing to bowling, dropping, and carving, there’s no shortage of excitement as we embark on this pumpkin demolition journey together. Bring along your leftover Halloween pumpkins or use some of ours – the choice is yours! So, gather your friends and family, and get ready to make memories. Let the smashing begin! Festival Highlights: Pumpkin Smashing Pumpkin Bowling Pumpkin Putt-Putt Pumpkin Chucking A HUGE Pumpkin Drop at 5:00pm! Live Music Local Winery & Brewery The excitement continues after dark with a glow in the dark pumpkin drop at 7pm and Fireworks at 8:30pm! Farm: 10am – 10pm Festival Activities: 1pm – 6pm Fireworks: 8:30pm Additional Fun Things To Do in Lancaster? discovery-95a925a5469240b52dfdac468bfc02.description: Thank you to all who came out for Fall Fest this year. North Museum and Millport Conservancy are grateful for your contribution to STEM education and environmental conservation in 2026! Fall Fest is an ongoing collaboration between two outstanding non-profits and is a fundraising event to support both STEM education programming at North Museum, and Millport Conservancy’s efforts to restore the Lititz Run through soil erosion control and stream management. VENUE Millport Conservancy 737 E Millport Rd, Lititz, PA 17543

Join us on select Friday evenings and Saturdays for toe-tapping tunes from our favorite bands. Mackenzie Paige is originally from a farm in Lancaster, Pennsylvania. She was raised in a very musical family, and began songwriting and performing at a young age. She went on to study music at Messiah University. Mackenzie was blessed to spend a semester of college at the Contemporary Music Center in Nashville, Tennessee. She has gleaned from artists such as Norah Jones, Miranda Lambert, and Natalie Hemby. She is a lover of all music, but country has stolen her heart, and feels like home. Additional Fun Things To Do in Lancaster? discovery-61761c44d771ebe6d3bd0bafd3dd8a.title: Preschool Picassos at North Museum
discovery-61761c44d771ebe6d3bd0bafd3dd8a.description: Calling all parents and caregivers with preschool-aged children who love to create art! Happening the first Saturday of every month, Preschool Picassos provides young visitors with a unique art experience when we teach children various science-based techniques with their caregivers. As children experiment and explore, they will not only learn to be a part of the conversation around Science, Technology, Engineering, Art, and Math (STEAM), but they will create some unique works of art along the way! Facilitator Marilyn Zenko has a background in STEM as an archeologist and is currently a Senior Client Development Specialist at Terracon. Enter with General Admission. $13 each. Free for Members. Kindly PRE-REGISTER so we can prepare the right materials. COME FOR PRESCHOOL PICASSOS, STAY FOR THE PLANETARIUM SHOW. 11am—One World, One Sky, Big Bird’s Adventure.

occurrences.title: Preschool Picassos at North Museum
occurrences.description: Calling all parents and caregivers with preschool-aged children who love to create art! Happening the first Saturday of every month, Preschool Picassos provides young visitors with a unique art experience when we teach children various science-based techniques with their caregivers. As children experiment and explore, they will not only learn to be a part of the conversation around Science, Technology, Engineering, Art, and Math (STEAM), but they will create some unique works of art along the way! Facilitator Marilyn Zenko has a background in STEM as an archeologist and is currently a Senior Client Development Specialist at Terracon. Enter with General Admission. $13 each. Free for Members. Kindly PRE-REGISTER so we can prepare the right materials. COME FOR PRESCHOOL PICASSOS, STAY FOR THE PLANETARIUM SHOW. 11am—One World, One Sky, Big Bird’s Adventure.

discovery-5214aac526b9462930b1f526140a1f.description: Step into the glow, where candlelight, harmony, and the beauty of the holiday season surround you. This intimate experience returns newly imagined — beloved songs reborn in-the-round by radiant performers and rich live music. Every seat is wrapped in warmth and wonder, offering moments of peace and a welcome rise of joy in the midst of the season’s rush. Immerse yourself in this soul-stirring concert that reminds us of what still feels sacred and leaves you carrying a little more light with you. discovery-b66df746894184cecdc6d0d25c525f.title: Thanksgiving Day Tour with Strasburg Scooter Tours
discovery-b66df746894184cecdc6d0d25c525f.description: What better way to relax before “Crazy Uncle Harvey” arrives and the feasting begins on Thanksgiving Day. Enjoy a ride on a 50cc scooter to visit 19th-century covered bridges with an experienced guide. This tour offers exceptional views of the countryside, including Amish farms and schoolhouses, as well as an insightful look at one of Lancaster County’s oldest covered bridges. This tour will give you a uniquely exciting way to get back in touch with historic Pennsylvania. Itinerary Duration: 2-3 hours Some of our past tours have included: A guided tour of two of Lancaster County’s most beautiful covered bridges A ride through Lancaster’s backcountry road during the loveliest time of year. Each year is unique, so you never know what we might have in store for you!

discovery-431a127829edc5f4cf757b9e0a98b2.title: Holiday Tasting Tour – Kitchen Kettle Village
discovery-431a127829edc5f4cf757b9e0a98b2.description: Sip, snack & shop your way through the Village Reserve the Holiday Flavors Self-Guided Tasting Tour Package for just $25*! Don’t miss our ONLY Holiday Tasting Tour of the season on Friday evening, November 27th. Enjoy the tree lighting, live music, holiday shopping, and lots of sampling. The Holiday Tasting Tour runs from 3-7pm, and offers three check-in times at 3pm, 3:30pm, and 4pm. Guests should arrive no later than 5pm. Check in on the porch of The Olive Basin to obtain your tasty passport and other surprises. Your culinary adventure includes stops at participating foodie locations and shops in the Village. Embrace the holiday season and make shopping fun with our Holiday Tasting Tour. Enjoy generous samples, personalized service, and bites of village history. You won’t want to miss this festive tasting experience for food lovers of all ages! Please note: we will try our best to make accommodations for dietary restrictions. When booking your reservation, be sure to fill out the allergies section. Reservations must be made in advance to enjoy this scrumptious event and can be completed online or by calling 1-800-732-3538 to reserve your spot. Reservations are non-refundable. •$25 per package + tax and booking fee Book Now

discovery-928ce639ed00fd56c355561b6595b4.title: Mixtape: Ali Murphy & Joshua William Green at Prima
discovery-928ce639ed00fd56c355561b6595b4.description: For years, Ali Murphy has led from the keys at the heart of Prima’s most iconic experiences. As pianist and music director of ILLUMINATION and numerous other productions, she has shaped the emotional architecture of the room with precision and artistry. Joshua William Green brings rich baritone depth and unmistakable presence. A frequent Prima director who steps into the spotlight when called, he carries both musical craftsmanship and warmth. Together, they curate a mixtape of songs that influenced their journeys — revealing the roots behind the sound audiences have come to love. At this time, the Mixtape Series is available exclusively as a two-show subscription at a special subscriber rate. Individual show tickets may be released at a later date, based on availability. Get more info about the Mixtape and purchase the series subscription below. discovery-1e5553781e29756cfbb84a35b053b3.title: Coterie Book Club
discovery-1e5553781e29756cfbb84a35b053b3.description: Join us for engaging discussions and a shared love of reading! The Coterie Book Club gathers monthly to explore a diverse range of titles, from historical fiction to gripping true crime. Whether you’re a lifelong reader or looking to get back into the habit, all are welcome. Coterie Book Club meets the third Tuesday of each month from 1-2pm Registration is encouraged September: Daughter of Egypt by Marie Benedict October: The Lion Women of Tehran by Marjan Kamali November: An American Girl by Richard Fellinger January: Theo of Golden by Allen Levi February: The Measure by Nikki Erlick March: The Correspondent by Virginia Evans April: The Beast in the Clouds by Nathalia Holt May: The Lies They Told by Ellen Marie Wiseman
discovery-1e5553781e29756cfbb84a35b053b3.location: Manheim Township Library, MTP Morgan Center A, 595 Granite Run Drive,  Lancaster, PA, 17601

discovery-f50ad8b6bb75f535a2beae7fe736ab.title: Chills, Thrills and that Spooky Stuff: Horror of the Early '60s with Kevin Stairiker!
discovery-f50ad8b6bb75f535a2beae7fe736ab.description: What keeps you up at night? 🌙 Horror movies have been trying to crack that spooky code for over a century! Styles may change, but a classic jump-scare can still creep out a fresh generation of moviegoers. 🎬 This October, test your brave side with us! 🎃 Every Tuesday night starting at 6pm, we’re screening legendary fright flicks that have given movie lovers the wiggles, the willies, and full-blown goosebumps for decades. 🍿 Hosted by Kevin Stairiker (LNP | LancasterOnline), each evening packs in creepy cinema, post-movie chats, light snacks, and maximum eerie vibes. 🕷️ Bring your courage (and a friend to hide behind)! 👀✨ October 5th: City of the Dead, 1960, 78 minutes October 20th: Black Sabbath, 1963, 93 minutes October 28th: The Innocents, 1961, 100 minutes Registration is encouraged!
discovery-f50ad8b6bb75f535a2beae7fe736ab.location: Manheim Township Library, MTP Morgan Center B, 595 Granite Run Drive,  Lancaster, PA, 17601

discovery-a99aefc9876e00db4af545394ab351.title: Decoding the Deck, Part 2: A Deep Dive into the Major Arcana
discovery-a99aefc9876e00db4af545394ab351.description: 🎨 Decoding the Deck, Part 2: A Deep Dive into the Major Arcana 🔮 Ready to take your Tarot knowledge to the next level? Join us for Part 2 of our educational Tarot series with local instructor Theresa from @claritymindretreat! 🃏✨ This time, we’re doing a deep dive into the 22 Major Arcana cards-- often known in art and literature as "The Fool’s Journey." Whether you attended Part 1 or are just jumping in now, this session will give you a much deeper appreciation for the visual storytelling hidden in the deck. 🎨🏛️ What we'll cover: 🃏 The Fool’s Journey: The narrative arc connecting the 22 Major Arcana cards. 🏛️ Universal Archetypes: The history and symbolism behind iconic cards like The Empress, The Lovers, and The World. 👁️‍🗨️ Visual Storytelling: How Renaissance art, allegory, and myth shaped the imagery we see today. Whether you're looking to decode your own deck or just love a fascinating deep-dive into art history, this class is for you! 📚✍️ ⚠️ Please note: This presentation is strictly educational and focused entirely on history, art, and symbolism. No live readings will be conducted!
discovery-a99aefc9876e00db4af545394ab351.location: Manheim Township Library, MTP Morgan Center C, 595 Granite Run Drive,  Lancaster, PA, 17601

discovery-da38552aeae679f9c26e2182051771.title: Bad Art Club
discovery-da38552aeae679f9c26e2182051771.description: Whether you’re a seasoned creative struggling with art block or an arts enthusiast who's never picked up a pencil. Bad Art Club encourages you to release your fears, doubts and/or perfectionistic tendencies. Instead, give yourself permission to play, make mistakes, have fun, and just make bad art. THANK YOU for registering -- it will help us determine how many supplies we need! · Ages 18+ Monthly Projects: January: A game of Pictionary (to celebrate the first club meet-up) February: Collage Night: Our Inner Garden March: Paint and Swap Night April: Found Poetry May: Play with Clay Dough June: Blind Contour Art Challenge July: Painted Paper Collage August: Zine Night (Theme: “Current Obsessions) September: Blind Contour Portraits October: Exquisite Corpse November: DIY mini card deck December: -No Meetup- January: Vision Bingo Cards

discovery-53fc2fe1049f57b417cf7123027ff0.title: Color & Chill
discovery-53fc2fe1049f57b417cf7123027ff0.description: The Sensory Social is getting a low-key summer remix! Drop in for a relaxing hour of coloring, lo-fi beats, and calm lighting. This is a self-guided, community-wide lounge where everyone is welcome to relax, keep their hands busy, and create at their own pace. Our space is intentionally designed to be sensory-friendly, fully accessible, and inclusive for all adults, including individuals with IDD, autism, and their support people. We provide a variety of intricate coloring pages, high-quality markers, and pens, but feel free to bring your own favorite supplies if you prefer! Come as you are, bring a friend, and just zone out and chill.
discovery-53fc2fe1049f57b417cf7123027ff0.location: Manheim Township Library, MTP Morgan Center B, 595 Granite Run Drive,  Lancaster, PA, 17601

discovery-266f9f888ed786bf8a6f97d1c8bbbd.description: Looking for a spook-tacular night out? Join us at the library after hours for a festive evening of adult trivia! Gather a team of up to six to test your knowledge on everything from classic horror literature and iconic spooky movies to haunted history and urban legends. We’ll supply the hot apple cider, seasonal treats, and prizes for the winning team-- plus bonus points if your team wears costumes! 🎃☕ Registration is required per team. discovery-776e7cd8e417288ad258723e575894.title: DNA & Dead Ends: Cracking Family Mysteries
discovery-776e7cd8e417288ad258723e575894.description: DNA doesn't lie! Eric Schubert will share real-life past examples from his work as a professional genealogist and forensic genetic genealogist which includes long-lost family discoveries and historic cold case breakthroughs. Attendees will learn practical strategies for starting or advancing their own research, from record paper trails to working with DNA matches. This program will offer a narrative of Eric’s research journey, as well as clear, accessible guidance for beginners and those with specific genealogical questions. These tips are inspired by experience solving complex cases for thousands across the country! Ages 18+ Space is limited · Registration is required
discovery-776e7cd8e417288ad258723e575894.location: Lancaster Library, LPL Board Room, 151 North Queen Street, Lancaster, PA, 17603

discovery-215eb0c201665129588c4ae7d7e41d.title: MTPL Plant Swap!
discovery-215eb0c201665129588c4ae7d7e41d.description: 🌱 MANHEIM TOWNSHIP PUBLIC LIBRARY PLANT SWAP & GARDENING PROGRAM 🌱 Whether you’re a seasoned plant parent or just looking to grow your collection, join us at the Manheim Township Public Library for a double dose of plant fun! Start by refreshing your garden at our community plant swap, and stay right after for an exciting, free gardening program to learn the secrets hidden in your landscape. How the Swap Works: Give One, Get One: Bring a healthy, pest-free plant (potted or a rooted cutting in a jar) to the swap table and take home a new green friend! 🌿🪴 Share the Knowledge: Feel free to attach care instructions or ID tags so the new owner knows how to help their new sprout thrive. Branch Out: Meet fellow local gardeners and swap expert tips along with your plants! Bonus Program Right After! Stick around immediately following the swap for The Treachery of Botany: Poisonous Garden Plants, a free, eye-opening session on identifying and managing hidden plant hazards in your landscape. Bring a plant, pick up a new favorite, and gain the know-how to keep your botanical sanctuary thriving and safe!
discovery-215eb0c201665129588c4ae7d7e41d.location: Manheim Township Library, MTP Morgan Center C, 595 Granite Run Drive,  Lancaster, PA, 17601

discovery-0aa99567cfb116d334389617344afe.title: The Treachery of Botany: Poisonous Garden Plants
discovery-0aa99567cfb116d334389617344afe.description: 🌿 BEAUTY OR BANE? THE SECRET LIFE OF YOUR GARDEN 💀 Vibrant lavender and mauve blossoms sway in the breeze while butterflies dip and dance above. With every rustle of foliage, delicate white buds flash in the sunlight. It’s the ultimate dream landscape—an idyllic, peaceful sanctuary designed for pure relaxation. But look closer. Hidden within this botanical paradise, unexpected danger might be lurking right in plain sight. Is that vivid red berry harmless or a hazard? What secret is that unusual violet flower stalk hiding? Could your pet's favorite sunbathing spot be surrounded by toxic greenery? Uncover the truth behind the beauty! Join speakers Cynthia Trussell, Indigo Bowser, and Kathy Vu of the Penn State Master Gardeners for The Treachery of Botany: Poisonous Garden Plants. In this eye-opening 45-minute presentation (followed by a Q&A session), you'll learn how to identify ordinary, uncommon, cultivated, and wild poisonous plants in your landscape-- discover what makes them tick, and master easy, practical ways to manage them safely. Keep your loved ones safe while keeping your sanctuary gorgeous. Don't miss it-- turn your garden into a true, worry-free paradise!
discovery-0aa99567cfb116d334389617344afe.location: Manheim Township Library, MTP Morgan Center B, 595 Granite Run Drive,  Lancaster, PA, 17601

discovery-41603b66d27b5fe37cae1f6a650915.title: Swoon Squad: A Romance TBR Book Club
discovery-41603b66d27b5fe37cae1f6a650915.description: Swoon Squad is a romance-centered book club with a twist. Instead of everyone reading the same assigned title, we choose a monthly trope and invite you to pick any book that fits the theme! Whether you're into sweet contemporary rom-coms, high-heat historical reads, or paranormal romance, there's a seat for you at our table! How it Works: Pick Your Own Adventure: We announce the month's trope, and you choose a book from your own TBR pile or the library shelves that features it. Low Pressure, High Fun: No more scrambling to finish a specific book you might not even like. Read at your own pace and bring your honest thoughts! The Discussion: We gather to swap recommendations, vent about our favorite (and least favorite) clichés, and discover new authors through each other's picks. Come ready to share your pick, discuss the tropes, and meet fellow romance fans in a comfortable library setting ❤️ June 29 - ⚔️Enemies to Lovers ⚔️ July 27 - 🥰😠Grumpy/Sunshine😠🥰 August 31 - 🏆Sports Romance🏆 September 28 - 📖Academic Romance📖 October 26 - 🧛Paranormal Romance🧛 November 30 - 🛏️Forced Proximity🛏️ December 28 - 🎁Holiday Romance🎁
discovery-41603b66d27b5fe37cae1f6a650915.location: Manheim Township Library, MTP Morgan Center A, 595 Granite Run Drive,  Lancaster, PA, 17601

Instead of everyone reading the same assigned title, we choose a monthly trope and invite you to pick any book that fits the theme! Whether you're into sweet contemporary rom-coms, high-heat historical reads, or paranormal romance, there's a seat for you at our table! How it Works: Pick Your Own Adventure: We announce the month's trope, and you choose a book from your own TBR pile or the library shelves that features it. Low Pressure, High Fun: No more scrambling to finish a specific book you might not even like. Read at your own pace and bring your honest thoughts! The Discussion: We gather to swap recommendations, vent about our favorite (and least favorite) clichés, and discover new authors through each other's picks. Come ready to share your pick, discuss the tropes, and meet fellow romance fans in a comfortable library setting ❤️ June 29 - ⚔️Enemies to Lovers ⚔️ July 27 - 🥰😠Grumpy/Sunshine😠🥰 August 31 - 🏆Sports Romance🏆 September 28 - 📖Academic Romance📖 October 26 - 🧛Paranormal Romance🧛 November 30 - 🛏️Forced Proximity🛏️ December 28 - 🎁Holiday Romance🎁
occurrences.categories: Book Club
occurrences.location: Manheim Township Library, MTP Morgan Center A, 595 Granite Run Drive,  Lancaster, PA, 17601
occurrences.price: Free

discovery-5a9a9b2bc0c697d68940aa2fd1b41e.title: Common Thread Crafting Club
discovery-5a9a9b2bc0c697d68940aa2fd1b41e.description: Unravel your creativity and connect at Common Thread Crafting Club! Whether you’re a master of the needles or just starting your first row, join our bimonthly gathering for all things fiber. From knitting and crochet to felting and cross-stitch, bring your current project and enjoy an afternoon of shared patterns, helpful tips, and great conversation. No matter your craft, we’re all tied together by a love for making. Registration is not required

discovery-14d3ee835b2ea95cdec2687a031833.title: Cooks & Books: Baking Techniques & Equipment Swap
discovery-14d3ee835b2ea95cdec2687a031833.description: Get your rolling pins ready! This month, Cooks & Books is getting a head start on the festive season by focusing on baking techniques to help level up your holiday spread. To inspire your baking, we’re drawing from two fantastic resources: Billy Parisi’s Website: Perfect for those who love detailed, chef-driven techniques and classic methods. Chasing Flavors by Dan Kluger: A deep dive into how flavor profiles work to make your bakes truly stand out. Bonus Special Event: We’ll also be hosting a Baking Tools & Equipment Swap! Bring any new or gently used kitchen gadgets, tools, or baking supplies (like rolling pins, specialty pans, or decorative sprinkles) you'd like to trade with fellow home cooks. Cooks & Books is a welcoming space for anyone who loves food and cooking. Bring a dish inspired by holiday baking techniques, your own place setting/to-go container, and a friend to join the conversation! Requirements: Attendees should be 14 years of age or older. Vegan and vegetarian recipes are always welcome. Supplies: Please bring your own serving utensils, place setting, to-go container, and beverage. Cost: The event is free, but reservations are required!
discovery-14d3ee835b2ea95cdec2687a031833.location: Manheim Township Library, MTP Morgan Center A, 595 Granite Run Drive,  Lancaster, PA, 17601

discovery-edde8108c168cce9481ac0bcbe2f3c.title: Game of Tomes Fantasy Book Club
discovery-edde8108c168cce9481ac0bcbe2f3c.description: Escape into another world with our fantasy book club! This book club is for anyone who enjoys fantasy or is looking to explore the genre for the first time. discovery-1bece5119be7a5e919858c5bb6f0ab.title: Coaching Inclusion
discovery-1bece5119be7a5e919858c5bb6f0ab.description: Why Inclusion is Good Business with Jane Horan Most leaders believe their team is inclusive, but their team often see it differently. Drawing on case studies and coaching stories from Coaching Inclusion, this talk makes the business case for inclusion in plain terms: better decisions, stronger retention, and helping leaders access the full range of expertise in the room. The book and talk reframe inclusion as a daily leadership practice, and participants experience one of the key elements of inclusion through a short listening and questioning exercise developed through years of coaching leaders across industries and cultures. Walk-ins welcome Ages 18+

discovery-9a7938a3d8fa05b12f526f7f3fbc18.title: MTPL Book Discussion Group
discovery-9a7938a3d8fa05b12f526f7f3fbc18.description: Start your Wednesday with a side of storytelling. The MTPL Book Discussion Group meets the 2nd Wednesday of each month at 10am to explore new worlds together. It’s more than just a book club—it’s your monthly morning retreat for thoughtful talk and local connection. We’ve got the books; we just need you! Please register for each meeting, as it allows the library to update you if there are any changes to a meeting due to weather delays, closures, or other circumstances. January 14: 1984 by George Orwell February 11: Empire of AI by Karen Hao March 11: The Greatest Generation by Tom Brokaw April 8: West with Giraffes by Lynda Rutledge May 13: Klara and the Sun by Kazuo Ishiguro June 10: Everything is Tuberculosis by John Green July 8: Kindred by Octavia Butler August 12: There Is No Place for Us by Brian Goldstone September 9: The Secret History by Donna Tartt October 14: On Call by Anthony Fauci November 11: Harlem Shuffle by Colson Whitehead December 9: The Frozen River by Ariel Lawhon
discovery-9a7938a3d8fa05b12f526f7f3fbc18.location: Manheim Township Library, MTP Morgan Center A, 595 Granite Run Drive,  Lancaster, PA, 17601

New members are welcome to join the discussion. 2027 Reading List January 14: Love in the Time of Cholera by Gabriel Garcia Marquez February 11: Jazz by Toni Morrison March 11: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest by Ken Kesey April 8: The Death of the Heart by Elizabeth Bowen May 13: Bel-Ami by Guy de Maupassant June 10: Blood Meridian by Cormac McCarthy July 8: Blindness by Jose Saramago August 12: The Kingdom and the Power by Gay Talese September 9: The Quiet American by Graham Greene October 14: A Tale of Two Cities by Charles Dickens November 18*: The Song of the Lark by Willa Cather December 9: Jayber Crow by Wendell Berry *Meeting a week later due to LPL's closure on Thursday, November 11.
occurrences.categories: Book Club
occurrences.location: Lancaster Library, LPL Board Room, 151 North Queen Street, Lancaster, PA, 17603
occurrences.price: Free

discovery-f98a788a68bb73b7c99414dcbfc3db.title: Mills of Lancaster County: An Afternoon with Historian Donald Kautz
discovery-f98a788a68bb73b7c99414dcbfc3db.description: Step back in time with author Donald Kautz and the Manheim Township Historical Society as we explore the history of Lancaster County’s water-powered grist mills. From the ingenious engineering of the waterwheel to the personal stories of the families who kept them running, this presentation brings our local heritage to life. Join us to discover the secret history of these iconic structures and see how they continue to shape our landscape today.
discovery-f98a788a68bb73b7c99414dcbfc3db.location: Manheim Township Library, MTP Morgan Center AB, 595 Granite Run Drive,  Lancaster, PA, 17601

discovery-9f193cf71a3b301fd8abed978abd6b.title: Marching to Independence: Lancaster Soldiers at the Battle of Fort Lee
discovery-9f193cf71a3b301fd8abed978abd6b.description: How did ordinary men from Lancaster County end up on the front lines of the American Revolution? Step back in time with living historian Samuel Leamer to uncover the harrowing story of Clotz's Battalion-- part of the legendary "Flying Camp" mobile reserve. Relive the tension of November 1776 at the Battle of Fort Lee, discover the courageous stories of local soldiers fighting for a brand-new nation, and see how modern historians uncover the past to keep their legacy alive. Don't miss this immersive journey into the fight for independence! Registration is encouraged! A Berks County native and Cairn University history graduate, Presenter Sam Leamer has spent a lifetime bringing the past to life through reenactments-- and a decade mastering the art of modern coffee. By blending historical scholarship with coffee expertise, Sam offers a richer, deeper look into Colonial Coffee Culture, showing how the humble coffee bean helped fuel America’s fight for independence.
discovery-9f193cf71a3b301fd8abed978abd6b.location: Manheim Township Library, MTP Morgan Center B, 595 Granite Run Drive,  Lancaster, PA, 17601

discovery-b2835165e32dc51095b0f0ff100c17.title: Well Rooted: Genealogy Drop In
discovery-b2835165e32dc51095b0f0ff100c17.description: Are you hitting a "brick wall" in your family tree research? Whether you are a seasoned researcher or just starting to wonder about your heritage, the library is here to help! Join us on the 3rd Thursday of every month at 3:00 PM for our Genealogy Drop-In Program. Our volunteers will be on hand to help you navigate databases, interpret census records, and organize your findings. If you have a specific research goal or a particularly tricky question, we encourage you to reach out to us ahead of time. Providing details in advance allows us to prepare resources specifically for your search. Send us an email at info@mtpl.info When: 3rd Thursdays at 3:00 PM Where: Morgan Center B Cost: Free and open to the public
discovery-b2835165e32dc51095b0f0ff100c17.location: Manheim Township Library, MTP Morgan Center B, 595 Granite Run Drive,  Lancaster, PA, 17601

discovery-8dd60812f1994e3fea700517275550.title: LPL Open Late: First Friday
discovery-8dd60812f1994e3fea700517275550.description: Make Lancaster Public Library a stop on your First Friday culture crawl! Downtown Lancaster springs to life on the First Friday of each month. Art galleries, studios, museums, restaurants, shops, and attractions in downtown Lancaster stay open late while people head out to enjoy the festive atmosphere, dining, art, and entertainment. Stop by the library to check out some books, browse the Juliana Bookstore, or find a quiet spot to sit and take it all in. We're open until 8PM on the following First Fridays: May 1 June 5 August 7 September 4 October 2 December 4

discovery-619d3222bf214b5a8e5d5ca6e03857.title: Coffee & Crossing: Washington's Winter of 1776
discovery-619d3222bf214b5a8e5d5ca6e03857.description: Grab a piping-hot mug of authentic colonial coffee and step right into the high-stakes winter of 1776! Join living historian Samuel Leamer to uncover the bold strategy, hidden Lancaster County connections, and dramatic reality behind Washington’s famous crossing of the Delaware and the epic 1st Battle of Trenton. Separate fact from fiction, sip historical brews, and discover how coffee and courage helped turn the tide of the Revolutionary War! Registration is encouraged A Berks County native and Cairn University history graduate, Sam Leamer has spent a lifetime bringing the past to life through reenactments-- and a decade mastering the art of modern coffee. By blending historical scholarship with coffee expertise, Sam offers a richer, deeper look into Colonial Coffee Culture, showing how the humble coffee bean helped fuel America’s fight for independence.
discovery-619d3222bf214b5a8e5d5ca6e03857.location: Manheim Township Library, MTP Morgan Center B, 595 Granite Run Drive,  Lancaster, PA, 17601

discovery-4476b5efc9b264ee6859e3e464cf85.title: Victorian Christmas: Customs & Costumes
discovery-4476b5efc9b264ee6859e3e464cf85.description: Step back in time and discover how many of our favorite holiday traditions began! Join historian Lynnette Miller from Landis Valley for a fascinating look into the holiday customs, festive decorations, and seasonal fashions of the Victorian era. From decorated evergreen trees and handmade gifts to period-appropriate winter attire, this presentation explores how Victorian-era families celebrated the holiday season. The presentation will be followed by a Q&A session with the audience. Free and open to the public. Registration is requested.
discovery-4476b5efc9b264ee6859e3e464cf85.location: Manheim Township Library, MTP Morgan Center B, 595 Granite Run Drive,  Lancaster, PA, 17601

discovery-0b74cae0507258597a6fead09bb9c1.title: The Neverland Book Club
discovery-0b74cae0507258597a6fead09bb9c1.description: The book club where our reading tastes never grow up! Every month, we'll discuss one middle-grade or young adult book. Here are just a few of the reasons to join: - Short books (easier to read before book club!) - Revisiting nostalgic stories or finding new favorites - Discussing meaningful topics and themes (you might be surprised by how deep children's literature can get!) Registration is encouraged, but walk-ins are welcome! Reading List: January 7: Bridge to Terabithia by Katherine Paterson February 4: Roll of Thunder, Hear My Cry by Mildred D. Taylor March 4: Redwall by Brian Jacques April 1: Speak by Laurie Halse Anderson May 6: The Outsiders by S. E. Hinton June 3: Matilda by Roald Dahl July 1: Holes by Louis Sachar August 5: Looking for Alaska by John Green September 2: A Wrinkle in Time by Madeleine L'Engle October 7: The Giver by Lois Lowry November 4: The Secret Garden by Frances Hodgson Burnett December 2: Charlotte's Web by E. B. White This is a book club for adults (ages 18+) to discuss children's books. For a list of children's programs at LPL, please check our events calendar.
discovery-0b74cae0507258597a6fead09bb9c1.location: Lancaster Library, LPL Board Room, 151 North Queen Street, Lancaster, PA, 17603

discovery-4cbca0703fe9ea4878ba9ed0d2149e.title: An Introduction to Poetry (For those who don’t like poetry)
discovery-4cbca0703fe9ea4878ba9ed0d2149e.description: Caroline Covington will give us a jump start on appreciating poems. Even those who already love poetry will “literally” enjoy an inspiring evening of ideas, tea, and finger foods. Ms. Covington (nee Nixon) is a Lancaster native, now living on Maryland's Eastern Shore. As an undergraduate she studied nursing, Bible, and music, and in graduate school, history. Along with a keen interest in the intellectual history of the Church Caroline also was introduced to the power of poetry during extended visits to English L'Abri, a residential study center in southern England. She currently fills her days gardening, knitting, cooking, talking on the phone with family and friends, and working alongside her husband, Will, caring for their 1790s home. And enjoying poetry, of course.
discovery-4cbca0703fe9ea4878ba9ed0d2149e.location: The Square Halo Gallery,37 North Market Street, Lancaster, PA 17603, USA

discovery-64d1703449a860bba31f9f44bc887c.title: Elvis Birthday Bash at American Music Theatre
discovery-64d1703449a860bba31f9f44bc887c.description: Elvis Birthday Bash with Mike Albert & Scot Bruce Mike Albert and Scot Bruce are widely considered the premier Elvis impersonators of our time, performing as the older and younger Elvis, respectively. Mike Albert’s Elvis tribute show has become known worldwide for the respectful portrayal of the late Elvis Presley. Mike has won several major world Elvis contests, and demand for his shows resulted in putting together a seven piece Big “E” Band to emulate the sound Elvis’ band had in the Vegas shows and on tour. Years ago, a part-time “gig” blossomed into a full-time career for Scot Bruce. Because of his uncanny resemblance to the young “King,” along with his ability to sing and strum a guitar, Scot’s live show has taken him all over the world. Scot has had the honor of performing with the legendary Jordanaires, Elvis’ original backup singers. Come experience AMT’s Elvis Birthday Bash and see why audiences are … All Shook Up! discovery-fb8cf270f39e53c3ce43d913d58554.title: The Places We Go II by Ross Junior Owusu
discovery-fb8cf270f39e53c3ce43d913d58554.description: December 4–January 29 • Regitz Gallery Opening Reception: Friday, December 4, 2026 • 5–8 p.m. The Places We Go II is a solo exhibition by Ghanaian mixed-media artist Ross Junior Owusu exploring migration as an interior and ongoing process of becoming. Through ceramics, assemblage, and mixed-media artwork, Owusu examines how memory, resilience, cultural identity, and belonging are carried, reshaped, and rebuilt across shifting landscapes. Using fragmented materials such as clay and reclaimed objects, Owusu presents migration not as a fixed journey of loss or arrival, but as a layered negotiation of selfhood. His sculptural works reflect the physical and emotional imprints of movement, exploring what is carried forward, what is left behind, and what endures. Clay serves as a central material and metaphor in Owusu’s practice, reflecting cycles of becoming, un-becoming, and re-becoming.
