discovery-9059b8df522a165ef606b9cd8995aa.title: McCaskey Combined Choirs – FREE
discovery-9059b8df522a165ef606b9cd8995aa.description: 6:30 pm • Steinman Hall Celebrate the vibrant sound of the J.P. McCaskey High School Combined Choirs in this free concert at the Ware Center in Lancaster. The ensemble, made up of the McCaskey Vocal Ensemble and McCaskey Voices of Freedom, will present a diverse program featuring both accompanied and a cappella choral music. To complement the evening’s art exhibit, the choirs will perform music from African culture, showcasing the students’ versatility and the range of musical styles they study throughout the school year, including both sacred and secular music. As J.P. McCaskey High School approaches its celebration of 90 years of choral music in Lancaster, come support these talented student singers and experience an evening of music, culture, and community. Admission: Free and open to the public! Accessibility: Sensory-friendly accommodations will be available. Please get in touch with Barry Kornhauser to learn more.

discovery-9e1a54696f539628fb20cacac00146.title: Overshare: I Did This for Me by Shauna L Yorty
discovery-9e1a54696f539628fb20cacac00146.description: November 6–24 • Regitz Gallery Opening Reception: Friday, November 6, 2026 • 5–8 p.m. Artist Talk: 6 p.m. Overshare: I Did This for Me is a raw, intimate body of work by Lancaster-based artist Shauna L Yorty, created over three years of survival, transformation, and self-discovery. Through cardboard collages and mixed media artwork, including dimensional pieces, Yorty explores the messy, hopeful, and deeply personal process of making art as a means of moving through difficult experiences. Yorty describes the exhibition as a culmination of three years of “survival, process, and expression in service of love.” The works are made from humble, everyday materials and embrace an intentionally raw, handmade aesthetic. Bright colors, bold forms, layered textures, and dimensional elements transform discarded materials into expressive works of contemporary art. Rather than creating art for perfection or approval, Yorty makes art as a way to process, connect, and keep moving forward. Overshare: I Did This for Me invites viewers to consider their own stories, vulnerabilities, and creative processes, while finding connection with others through artistic expression. About the Artist Shauna L Yorty is a Lancaster-based artist whose bright, bold artwork tells powerful stories of hope and healing. Working from a systems-thinking perspective, Yorty draws connections between a lifetime of experiences, passions, and joys to create opportunities for people to connect with themselves, one another, and their own stories through the process of making art together. Yorty’s artistic practice centers on participation, storytelling, and connection. Their work encourages people to own, tell, and participate in their own stories, reflecting a belief in art as a tool for personal expression, healing, and community.

discovery-bbaa00fa614fa94795bb98e1fa1a85.title: Prison Portrait Project by Carolyn Harper
discovery-bbaa00fa614fa94795bb98e1fa1a85.description: October 2–30 • Regitz Gallery Opening Reception: Friday, October 2, 2026 • 5–8 p.m. Artist Talk: 6 p.m. Carolyn Harper’s Portrait Prison Project brings the lives and humanity of incarcerated and formerly incarcerated individuals into focus through hand-sewn, large-format quilts and hand-embroidered batiks. Many of the people Harper portrays are serving life-without-parole sentences in Pennsylvania, and many have spent decades behind bars. Harper does not seek to determine the innocence or guilt of the people she portrays. Instead, her textile portraits of incarcerated people focus on their individuality, dignity, humanity, and capacity for transformation. She has intentionally avoided asking the people she knows about the crimes that led to their incarceration, allowing them to share their stories on their own terms. Through these relationships, Harper has come to focus on redemption, rehabilitation, and the ways people change over the course of their lives. Every stitch is painstakingly sewn by hand, reflecting the minutes, days, and years that make up a life spent behind bars. The beauty and craftsmanship of the quilts and embroidered batiks create a striking tension with the difficult realities experienced by their subjects, inviting viewers to consider the humanity of people who are often overlooked or forgotten. About the Artist Carolyn Harper is a textile artist, educator, and advocate whose work combines portraiture, textile art, social justice, and activism. Raised in Rochester, New York, Harper moved to Philadelphia in 1989 to attend the University of Pennsylvania, where she earned an MFA studying under artists Neil Welliver and Rafael Ferrer. Harper has worked as an arts administrator and educator and has long been involved in volunteer and advocacy work. For many years, she created panels for the AIDS NAMES Memorial Quilt Project, taught art classes in homeless shelters, and advocated for homeless and incarcerated populations. She currently teaches classes and workshops in textile art, portraiture, and social justice art. Her current artistic practice brings together art, advocacy, and activism.

Experiment with ways to transform everyday subjects into striking works of art! Registration: $45 All materials included.

discovery-544412c2f9dcfef8d9aa0560904b8e.title: Rock of Ages
discovery-544412c2f9dcfef8d9aa0560904b8e.description: University Theatre presents Rock of Ages, the hit musical featuring live music and classic songs by Styx, Journey, Bon Jovi, Whitesnake, Twisted Sister, and more. It is the tail end of the 1980s on Hollywood’s Sunset Strip, where aspiring rock star Drew dreams of taking the stage and falling in love with Sherrie, a small-town girl newly arrived in Los Angeles. When developers threaten to replace the Strip’s legendary rock venues with a shopping complex, Drew, Sherrie, and an unforgettable group of musicians, dreamers, and devoted rock fans must come together to save their beloved neighborhood. Packed with iconic songs, big personalities, and plenty of 1980s energy, Rock of Ages is a celebration of dreams, determination, and the music that defined a generation. MU Students can purchase up to one (1) discounted ticket for $5.00 with a valid MU ID. MU Discounts are NOT available online and must be purchased in-person or by calling any box office location. Venue has limited seating capacity. Advanced ticket reservations are strongly encouraged. MU Discount tickets are subject to availability at the door.

discovery-1d8fcf329eb85e3a6db97e5055fa63.title: Glorious Sounds of the Season
discovery-1d8fcf329eb85e3a6db97e5055fa63.description: This is the 21st annual performance of Glorious Sounds of the Season, a festive fundraiser presented by over 250 students and faculty from MU’s Tell School of Music. Proceeds support student scholarships and program development. Traditional holiday favorites are presented alongside a diverse and varied selection of world music. To create musical momentum and excitement, the concert is presented in a unique kaleidoscopic format. Performers are placed throughout the hall — with no applause between selections — creating seamless transitions and continuous music-making. This Millersville tradition is the perfect way to get into the holiday spirit! Be sure to purchase your tickets early, as performances often sell out. Ticket PricesAdvanced: $30.00 Day Of: $34.00 MU Student w/ID: $5.00* *MU Students will receive up to one (1) discounted ticket with a valid MU ID. MU discounts are NOT available online and must be made in-person or by calling any box office location. MU discount tickets are subject to availability on the day of the event.Advanced ticket reservations are strongly encouraged.

discovery-4a55251a7edd332110f62ae199bae7.title: Disposable Humanity – FREE
discovery-4a55251a7edd332110f62ae199bae7.description: Tuesday, November 17, 2026 • 7 PM • Steinman Hall In Disposable Humanity, the Mitchell family—esteemed Disability Studies scholars and filmmakers—delve into the chilling legacy of the Nazi Aktion T4 program. This investigative documentary recounts the long-obscured history of how over 300,000 disabled individuals became the initial victims of the Third Reich. Targeted by the T4 program as having a “life unworthy of living,” their murders laid the groundwork for the Holocaust that followed. 6:15 PM • Pre-show community panel discussion Post-show • Q&A with director Cameron Mitchell Accessibility: The film is captioned, and live captioning (CART) and ASL interpreting will be provided for the panel discussion. Please get in touch with Barry Kornhauser to learn more. Co-presented by the MU Disability Film Festival and Congregation Shaarai Shomayim.

discovery-bd218f07c8a10f719f3d8803a117f3.description: Friday, December 18, 2026 • 7:30 PM • Steinman Hall In Big Band history, the Tommy Dorsey Orchestra is recognized as one of the best all-around dance bands—it could swing with the best of them, and no other band could come close to Tommy’s when it came to creating warm, sentimental ballads. discovery-f32ce10879f2b20703094918fa31b1.title: The Hot Sardines – Holiday Stomp
discovery-f32ce10879f2b20703094918fa31b1.description: Wednesday, December 9, 2026 • 7:30 PM • Steinman Hall Jazz revivalists the Hot Sardines throw a raucous yuletide extravaganza inspired by classic holiday films (such as White Christmas and It’s a Wonderful Life) and timeless classics, with hat-tips to Louis Armstrong, Edith Piaf, Duke Ellington, and beyond. Get your season swinging with fresh takes on “Mistletoe and Holly,” “Le Noël de la Rue,” “Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy,” “Blue Christmas,” “Christmas Blues,” “White Christmas,” “Please Come Home for Christmas,” and more. Tickets: Adults $35 • Students: $25

discovery-b898c186fb9072c4700d85bdf93b81.title: LBBB presents “Our Best Brass Christmas”
discovery-b898c186fb9072c4700d85bdf93b81.description: Sunday, December 20 • 3:00 PM • Steinman Hall Lancaster British Brass Band consists of 31 players. It draws its personnel from the four state regions of Pennsylvania, Maryland, Delaware and New Jersey. Originally conceived as a top-level, professional quality ensemble, it includes among its membership professional solo and ensemble players and music teacher/performers. The band members bring years of playing and teaching experience to the organization from such diverse institutions as The United States Marine Band, and the Lancaster, Harrisburg, Reading and York Symphony Orchestras. Many players are currently engaged as teachers in various public and private school venues and in such institutions of higher learning as West Chester, Millersville and Kutztown Universities, Lebanon Valley College, and The University of Delaware. Tickets: $25

discovery-355465fc912456bd8f95cf74e1cec5.title: Mixtape: Ali Murphy & Joshua William Green
discovery-355465fc912456bd8f95cf74e1cec5.description: For years, Ali Murphy has led from the keys at the heart of Prima’s most iconic experiences. As pianist and music director of ILLUMINATION and numerous other productions, she has shaped the emotional architecture of the room with precision and artistry. Joshua William Green brings rich baritone depth and unmistakable presence. A frequent Prima director who steps into the spotlight when called, he carries both musical craftsmanship and warmth. Together, they curate a mixtape of songs that influenced their journeys — revealing the roots behind the sound audiences have come to love. Purchase individual tickets for each Mixtape performance, or bundle with the February Mixtape show and purchase a subscription to save! Get tickets Get Mixtape Subscription For Mixtape Concerts, libations are available for purchase at the in-theater bar. Stay in the loop: Sign up for Prima emails and be the first to know when tickets drop!

discovery-5ba6b3d7e9099cb7218b1839877496.title: Murder At Ackerton Manor
discovery-5ba6b3d7e9099cb7218b1839877496.description: The motives are absurd. The murders are frequent. The laughs are nonstop. On a dark and stormy night at Ackerton Manor, the loathed Roger Ackerton meets a deadly end. Enter Detective Pierre Pierrot, armed with only a corpse, a missing diamond, and five eccentric suspects — each with a motive more absurd than the last. In this whirlwind tribute to Agatha Christie, three actors bring seven outrageous characters to life. Twists, turns, and mistaken identities keep the laughs, and bodies, coming. A streamlined, freewheeling American adaptation of Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol that sends Scrooge from his childhood in England (at the Burberry Academy for Unloved Boys) to America to make his fortune after being spurned by the love of his life. This Scrooge riffs on the classic story with local references, irreverent humor, homemade magic, and lightning-fast quick changes that astound and delight. The joy of the show is watching a talented, funny cast of five navigate all the lunacy. discovery-d9acb30027e35f0e8d65a9a170cc1a.title: The Woman in Black
discovery-d9acb30027e35f0e8d65a9a170cc1a.description: The Woman in Black October 30-November 1, 2026 Prepare for a night of spine-tingling suspense with The Woman in Black, a chilling theatrical ghost story that has captivated audiences for decades. When a lawyer obsessed with a tragic event from his past enlists a young actor to help him tell his tale, what begins as a simple retelling soon blurs into a terrifying encounter with the supernatural. With only three actors and minimal staging, The Woman in Black conjures an atmosphere of creeping dread and mounting tension, proving that what you don’t see can haunt you the most.

discovery-2f67214baf3b5023001c146a4a6993.title: The Lion King KIDS
discovery-2f67214baf3b5023001c146a4a6993.description: reserve show tickets AGES 8-12 This camp is currently at cast capacity. Journey to the African savanna with The Lion King KIDS! This vibrant musical adventure brings to life the beloved story of Simba, a young lion who must find his courage and take his place as king. Filled with unforgettable songs like “Hakuna Matata” and “Circle of Life,” dazzling characters, and powerful themes of family and responsibility, The Lion King KIDS is a heartwarming celebration of love, bravery, and the circle of life itself. Perfect for audiences of all ages, this colorful production will have you roaring with joy! Rehearsals: October 13 - November 13 Performances:Saturday, November 14 at 1:00pm & 4:00pmat Calvary Baptist Church Please note: Our Kids shows are shorter in length and use minimal costumes, props, and sets. For a more fully staged experience, check out our Junior and Mainstage shows! Approximate run-time is 35 minutes. No intermission. Tickets are Pay-What-You-Will and all donations help support Servant Stage's Youth Theatre program! Auditions Auditions will be held on October 13 from 6-9pm during the first day of rehearsal. All students will audition and will be cast in the show, these auditions simply help the production team in assigning roles to the students. Rehearsals October 13 - November 13 (Location TBD) 6-8:30pm • Tuesdays, Thursdays & Friday, November 13 *note later end time for October 13 Tuition/Financial Aid See our Tiered Pricing Options. A non-refundable $25 fee is required for initial registration. Upon completion of this registration, a confirmation email requesting payment to secure the student's registration will be sent out and payment will be due by March 31. Youth Theatre Summer Camp costs include: T-shirt, all materials and handouts, rehearsals with the Servant Stage staff. Financial aid available! Apply now. Students will need to bring their own snacks, lunches, and water bottles. All students who register are expected to be able to attend all rehearsals and performances. No refunds will be issued within one month of the start of camp. THE LION KING KIDS is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI. www.MTIShows.com. back to Youth Theatre Home Touring locations and individual times are listed above or at the source. The advertised range is not a continuous performance.

Celebrate the season with Joy To The World—a beloved return of Servant Stage’s original Christmas revue! Bursting with festive music, joyful dancing, and heartwarming moments, this spirited show features favorite carols and holiday classics from around the world. With stunning harmonies, lively choreography, and a talented cast spreading cheer, Joy To The World is a celebration of hope, love, and the true meaning of Christmas. Perfect for the whole family, this joyous production will fill your heart with holiday spirit! discovery-a7c00aae42890dfd3d0a6a53cfc0ec.title: Honk! JR
discovery-a7c00aae42890dfd3d0a6a53cfc0ec.description: Ages 10-16 This production is currently at capacity. Sign Up For The Waitlist The beloved tale of Hans Christian Andersen’s The Ugly Duckling bursts into song in this charming musical adaptation about navigating our differences and finding where we belong. In Honk JR, Ugly isn’t quite like his darling duckling brothers and sisters—and he soon finds out that standing out in his barnyard world isn’t easy! When Ugly finds himself separated from his family, he sets out on an adventure filled with colorful new friendships, a conniving cat, and the discovery that what makes him different is also what makes him special! Bursting with color and fun, Honk JR is perfect for audiences of all ages! auditions December 7-8 held at Lancaster Alliance Church Following enrollment, all registered students should sign up for a 5-minute audition slot, which helps the production team play to everyone’s strengths in the distribution of roles and other show material. More details about auditions are included in the Welcome Letter sent about two months prior to the start of rehearsals. Rehearsal Schedule January 3-17 at Lancaster Alliance Church (210 Pitney Rd, Lancaster) January 18-21 at Smoketown Elementary School (500 Mt Sidney Rd, Lancaster) 6-9pm Mondays, Tuesdays, Thursdays 3-9pm Sundays Performances Performances take place at Smoketown Elementary School (500 Mt Sidney Rd, Lancaster, PA 17602). Friday, January 22 | 7pmSaturday, January 23 | 11am & 3pmSunday, January 24 | 3pm Approximate run-time is an hour and 15 minutes. No intermission. Tickets are Pay-What-You-Will and all donations help support Servant Stage's Youth Theatre program! Info on Tuition/Financial Aid See our Tiered Pricing Options. A non-refundable $25 fee is required for initial registration. Within a week of your enrollment, you will receive instructions to make full tuition payment and complete your registration through the new Servant Stage portal. Payment will be due by November 15. No refunds will be issued within one month of the start of camp (December 3). Youth Theatre Production costs include: T-shirt, all materials and handouts, rehearsals with the Servant Stage staff. If you need to apply for financial assistance, you can do so here. Additional Information Students will need to bring their own snacks, dinners, and water bottles. All students who register are expected to be able to attend all rehearsals and performances. Meet the Directors Danielle PoznanovicDirector HONK JR is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI. www.MTIShows.com. back to Youth Theatre Home Touring locations and individual times are listed above or at the source. The advertised range is not a continuous performance.

Party begins at 7:45 PM. (The pre-show party is 21+) To attend the Pre-Show Cocktail hour, guests must have a ticket to the show. This event is all ages – 21+ With Valid ID to Drink Come hungry! Snacks and light bites will be available at the canteen. ————————————————— Presented by Lindsay Bretz-Morgans Upfront Theatre ————————————————— Join us at Mickey’s Black Box as The Rocky Horror Show RETURNS for a 6th year! This cult phenomenon (the stage show came before the movie) traces the bizarre adventures of super-naive and innocent Brad Majors and Janet Weiss. Follow Brad and Janet as they try desperately to survive the diabolical Riff-Raff & his incestuously sexy sister Magenta, Columbia, Eddie, the – perfect creation – Rocky, Dr.Scott, Transylvanian servants and the worlds most powerful but sweet transvestite–a man simply referred to as Frank -n- Furter–who will change their lives and libidos forever. The Rocky Horror Show is presented through special arrangement with Concord Theatricals. ————————————————— *Ticket Alert* Tickets for Mickey’s Black Box are sold through TicketMaster, via our website, or in person at our Box Office. Any tickets purchased elsewhere will not be honored and we are not responsible for tickets purchased from any 3rd party sellers. Do not google the name of the band to search for tickets. Go to Mickeysblackbox.com ONLY. Mickeysblackbox.com will never direct you anywhere but the official TicketMaster event site. All bags are subject are to search upon entry. Tickets are non-refundable, save for instances in which performances are cancelled by Mickey’s Black Box. For more information about our venue or to make an ADA request, please visit the FAQ page of our website: https://mickeysblackbox.com/faq/ or call our box office line at (717) 723 – 8463.

discovery-59ac4d1c2b7a2ad0aaa837500931ff.description: Sunday November 1st, 2026 *EARLY SHOW* Doors | 2:30 PM Show | 3:00 PM General Admission Seating | $23.40 + Fees +$3 on All Day of Show Purchases Thanks to our generous sponsors – Student tickets are free of charge This event is all ages – 21+ With Valid ID to Drink Come hungry! Snacks and light bites will be available at the canteen. ————————————————– Presented by Mickey’s Black Box & Music For Everyone ————————————————– Jazz and blues vocalist Ava Preston is a rising star, gaining attention nationwide as an exceptional singer, composer and arranger. Ava will be accompanied by pianist Cameron Campbell, bassist Allison Lee and drummer Janae Yates. Just 21 years old, Ava this year won the 2026 Ella Fitzgerald International Jazz Vocal Competition and earned her master’s degree in jazz voice from Juilliard. During her middle school, high school and college years, Ava was a 12-time winner of the Student Music Award bestowed by DownBeat magazine — capturing the top Vocal Jazz Soloist honor six times and the top Blues/Pop/Rock Soloist honor six times. Ava is passionate about bringing live jazz to the public, creating in 2025 an ongoing initiative called “Sidewalk Swing: Bringing Jazz & Joy to Every Corner” that places combos of student musicians on the streets of Manhattan. “I believe that music is a universal language that can unite people around the world,” Ava says. “My hope is to move society in a positive direction with my art … My goal is to spread world tolerance and the acceptance of differences through my music.” Check out Ava Preston here! Forbidden will be released by BLKIIBLK Records and charts a defiant journey through scything riffs, incredible melodies, 24 karat lead guitars, simply thunderous drums and bass, plus the studio debut of Norman Skinner (Niviane & Imagika) whose soaring vocals elevate the material to unprecedented levels. When the band’s members crossed paths on Shakedown Street, something clicked – and the music hasn’t stopped since. Rather than imitating the Dead, Shakedown Citi channels their spirit – creating spontaneous, soulful performances that feel alive, adventurous and totally in the moment. Each set is a journey, full of unexpected twists, deep grooves and musical conversation that pulls even the most skeptical listener into the vibe. Every Shakedown Citi show begins long before the first note. Each setlist is thoughtfully and meticulously crafted from the Dead repertoire, affiliated catalogs and beyond, balancing deep cuts and beloved anthems, rarities and reprises. No two nights are ever the same – each performance stands as a work of art on its own, alive in its moment, while also fitting into the larger patchwork of the repertoire. discovery-e95a8227bf96b5ff1082bf20036729.description: Saturday November 28th, 2026 Doors | 7:00 PM Show | 8:00 PM General Admission Standing Room | $29.55 + Fees Reserved Balcony & Mezzanine Seating | $40.30 + Fees +$5 on All Day of Show Purchases This event is all ages – 21+ With Valid ID to Drink Come hungry! Snacks and light bites will be available at the canteen. ————————————————— Presented by Big Fan Presents ————————————————— The Small Town Titans return to Mickey’s Black Box for their annual Home Town Holiday Show! The Small Town Titans are an American rock n’ roll power trio from York, PA who love to constantly create, as well as play live. Gone is the notion that a rock band should only release 10 songs at a time every 2 years. In a world where music fans crave new content constantly, the Small Town Titans aim to deliver their brand of art all of the time, drawing inspiration from a newer wave of rock bands such as Highly Suspect and Royal Blood, and rock legends such as the Foo Fighters, Audioslave, and Deep Purple. Thanks to their efforts at taking matters into their own hands, STT can create and release songs, podcasts, live online concerts, and more with no rules. In a social media driven world, STT knows releasing quality, constant content is as important as playing great live shows. In November of 2018, the band’s cover of the Christmas song “You’re a Mean One, Mr. Grinch” went viral in a matter of days, leading to charting on various Billboard charts including Holiday Digital Song Sales, Rock Digital Song Sales, Emerging Artists, and reaching #5 on the Next Big Sound chart. The song also reached #2 on the iTunes Rock charts, only being surpassed by Queen’s “Bohemian Rhapsody”. STT quickly found themselves achieving success, all on their own terms. As a continued unsigned act, all three members have risen to the occasion to continue to make music the way they want to, free from having to follow traditional music industry rules. By changing their mindset and focus towards creating content like many successful YouTubers, STT has made fans the old fashioned way, by word of mouth. With no manager, label, or radio support, the Small Town Titans have managed to find success by simply never forgetting one thing, their fans, both new and old. Instead of trying to make a million fans, STT is focusing on the fans they already have, and the ones they continue to make. With a love for playing live, a Small Town Titans show has evolved into more than a concert. It’s an event, with a set list that’s decided right before the show, and plenty of stage banter in between songs. The band simply hits the stage to deliver an energy driven show using guitars, drums, and their voices. Nothing more, nothing less. This approach to their live performances has led to them sharing the stage with acts such as Highly Suspect, Papa Roach, Black Stone Cherry, Pop Evil, and more. Check out the Small Town Titans here! Snacks and light bites will be available at the canteen. ————————————————– Presented by Mickey’s Black Box ————————————————– It is a little-known fact that most Amish practice a tradition similar to the Christian “Confirmation” and Jewish “Bar Mitzvah” called “Rumspringa” (literal translation: “running around”) in which Amish children at the age of 16 have an opportunity to live free of the strict Amish code of conduct before deciding if they want to come back and be baptized into the Amish church. Surprisingly, virtually all of the youths return. But sometimes they don’t. Four out of the original six members of The Amish Outlaws were born and raised in Lancaster, PA and had a strict Amish upbringing. No electricity from land lines, no alcohol, no musical instruments, but their spirits were too wild for the Amish lifestyle. Once they trampled in the Devil’s Playground, there was no turning back. In the years since Rumspringa, the members of the Amish Outlaws have become very well acclimated to the pleasures and vices of the modern world… music, most of all. Hip hop, rock, country, metal, disco, opera. There is no genre they do not touch upon. Thus, with a bold lust for life and a fire for music and performance that can only come from 16 years of repression, The Amish Outlaws were unleashed upon the world. Snacks and light bites will be available at the canteen. ————————————————— Presented by Big Fan Presents ————————————————— After two decades, it would be all too easy for a band to just phone it in—capitalize on the fanbase they’ve built up in that time and just make a watered-down version of themselves. Not for The Early November, however. Ever since forming in New Jersey in 2001, the band, now consisting of frontman Ace Enders and founding drummer Jeff Kummer— have constantly been striving to find the best and most definitive version of themselves. With this self-titled record, the seventh studio album of their career, the duo have come as close as is possible to doing so. It’s an album that ties the past, present and future all together, and as such, it marks what Enders calls a “period or exclamation point in our sentence”. It’s not a new beginning, per se, but nevertheless something emphatic that signifies, in Enders’ words again, “a pivotal moment” for them both. Check out The Early November here! discovery-d0f5cb22f69e0c868e368a51050780.description: Friday January 8th, 2027 Doors | 7:00 PM Show | 8:00 PM General Admission Standing Room | $35.70 + Fees +$5 on All Day of Show Purchases This event is all ages – 21+ With Valid ID to Drink Come hungry! Snacks and light bites will be available at the canteen. ————————————————– Presented by Mickey’s Black Box ————————————————– BLURRYFACE is a tribute to Twenty One Pilots built by fans, for fans. Designed to capture the energy, emotion, and spectacle of a full Twenty One Pilots concert, BLURRYFACE delivers an up-close and personal live experience crafted specifically for intimate venues where the original band cultivated their passionate fanbase. Audiences get the rare feeling of being fully immersed in the music, the visuals, and the community that has made Twenty One Pilots one of modern music’s most dedicated fanbases. This is far more than a cover set. BLURRYFACE recreates the feeling of a modern Twenty One Pilots arena production inside a smaller, more personal environment. Featuring synchronized video content, dynamic lighting, programmed visuals, CO2 cannons, and carefully curated live moments, every aspect of the show is designed to capture the emotional highs, explosive energy, and atmosphere fans know and love. From massive singalongs to intimate moments of reflection, the goal is to make every audience member feel like they are part of something bigger than just a concert. At its core, BLURRYFACE exists to celebrate the music and the community surrounding it. The members of BLURRYFACE are massive Twenty One Pilots fans themselves, with a deep understanding of the connection this music creates for people. The band is not trying to imitate or pretend to be Twenty One Pilots. Instead, they aim to honor the experience that Tyler and Josh created by bringing fans together in a safe, welcoming environment where they can express themselves freely, celebrate the music they love, and share in the emotional connection that has always been at the heart of the Twenty One Pilots community. discovery-744369cc5c8e1c6310a215a223561c.title: Conewago Rec Trail Field Trip
discovery-744369cc5c8e1c6310a215a223561c.description: Carl Groff will lead this easy walking field trip west along the trail with a stop at the Hershey Trust Wetlands overlook, and then continue west with views of open fields, woodland, and creeks. The walk will be out and back, probably a distance of 2-3 miles, depending on the wishes of the group. You may turn around at any time to go back to the parking lot. Note: You can no longer park along Rt. 743. From Lancaster take Rt. 283 west to the Elizabethtown Rt. 743 exit. Turn right onto Rt. 743 towards Hershey. Go about 1/4 mile and turn right on Beverly Road. A parking area for the Conewago Trail is on the left side of the road at Old Trolley Line Park. There is a porta-john in the parking lot. Meet Carl at 8 a.m. in the parking lot and bring water and snacks. Contact Carl at (717-471-9969 or fledge19@verizon.net) by 6 p.m. the day before if you have questions or would like to attend. Meeting Location: Old Trolley Line Park, 475 Beverly Rd., Elizabethtown, PA 17022 Contact: Carl Groff (717) 471-9969 or fledge19@verizon.net

discovery-3d108449435d6587f4dffbea2aff76.title: Monthly Club Meeting – “In Search of 10,000, and 10,000, and 10,000 Birds”
discovery-3d108449435d6587f4dffbea2aff76.description: Club Meeting – North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA 17603 Presented by Peter Kaestner, legendary birder and retired diplomat Peter Kaestner relates his life-long quest to see 10,000 species of birds – a quest that was almost derailed on February, 2024, when another birder claimed the record just hours before Peter saw is last bird in the Philippines. Since then, Peter has maintained his quest, ultimately observing 10,000 species in the eBird and AviList taxonomies. Peter is a retired U.S. diplomat and an active independent birder who has spent a lifetime sharing his passion. On February 9, 2024, he achieved his ultimate goal when he saw his 10,000th species of bird, an Orange-tufted Spiderhunter in Mindanao, the Philippines on the IOC taxonomy. On October 21, 2025, he reached 10,000 on eBird, and on November 11, 2025, he recorded his 10,000th species on the new AviList harmonized world bird list. Always a birder, Peter took his first international trip at age ten, when he visited the Bahamas with his brother and mentor Hank. As of December 2025, he has birded in 196 eBird countries and territories. He is recognized by the Guinness Book of Records for having the world’s biggest life lists eBird (10022) and AviList (10,008) and as the first person to see a representative of every bird family – a feat that he accomplished in October, 1986. The highlight of Peter’s birding career came in 1989. Just 50 kilometers east of the Colombian capital, he discovered a bird new to science, the Cundinamarca Antpitta (Grallaria kaestneri). Peter graduated from Friends School Baltimore, where he received the William S. Pike science award and all-state honors in lacrosse. He studied Biology at Cornell University, graduating in 1976. Peter served in the Peace Corps in Zaire (Democratic Republic of Congo) as a secondary-school science teacher in 1976-1978 and joined the U.S. Department of State in June, 1980. During his 36-year career as a U.S. diplomat, he helped negotiate the UN Desertification Convention and a protocol amending the 1916 Migratory Bird Convention with Canada. He represented the United States at Conferences of the Parties of the Ramsar Convention and CITES. Peter has lived in 12 different countries: India, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, USA, Colombia, Malaysia, Namibia, Guatemala, Brazil, Egypt, Afghanistan, and Germany. Peter retired in 2016 from the State Department at the rank of Minister-Counselor. Peter loves sharing his passion for birds by writing articles, leading bird walks and tours, supporting local conservation efforts, and giving illustrated lectures on birds around the world. After the Colombian Government made peace with the FARC guerilla group, Peter helped it bring economic development to rural areas by promoting bird tourism. He also worked with the American Bird Conservancy and a Colombian NGO (Fundación Camaná) to preserve critical habitat of the Cundinamarca Antpitta in the east Andes. In 2019, Peter became a part-time tour leader for Rockjumper Birding Tours, in 2021 he became a VIP for Swarovski Optik, in 2023 he was appointed ambassador of the American Bird Conservancy, and in 2024 he received the American Birding Association’s Roger Tory Peterson Lifetime Achievement Award. Peter is married to Kimberly Vreeland Kaestner, and has two grown daughters, Laurel and Katie.

Peter loves sharing his passion for birds by writing articles, leading bird walks and tours, supporting local conservation efforts, and giving illustrated lectures on birds around the world. After the Colombian Government made peace with the FARC guerilla group, Peter helped it bring economic development to rural areas by promoting bird tourism. He also worked with the American Bird Conservancy and a Colombian NGO (Fundación Camaná) to preserve critical habitat of the Cundinamarca Antpitta in the east Andes. In 2019, Peter became a part-time tour leader for Rockjumper Birding Tours, in 2021 he became a VIP for Swarovski Optik, in 2023 he was appointed ambassador of the American Bird Conservancy, and in 2024 he received the American Birding Association’s Roger Tory Peterson Lifetime Achievement Award. Peter is married to Kimberly Vreeland Kaestner, and has two grown daughters, Laurel and Katie.

discovery-46adf2dc0c9d1d5d1606ba7471b793.title: Monthly Club Meeting – “Wearables for Wildlife: Behind the Scenes with the Evolution of Wildlife Telemetry Technologies”
discovery-46adf2dc0c9d1d5d1606ba7471b793.description: Club Meeting – North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA 17603 Presented by Club President Andy McGann Andy McGann grew up birding in Southcentral Pennsylvania and his early experiences ultimately led to a career in the field of Movement Ecology. His time in academia, non-profits, consulting, and ultimately to a wildlife telemetry tech company spanned a timeframe that saw the science advance from analog radio telemetry to “smart devices” with GPS, accelerometers, and global Internet connectivity. In his career, Andy combined his experiences in ornithology with his love of technology and appreciation for geography in order to help wildlife researchers and organizations around the world obtain the scientific information needed to help conserve some of the rarest birds we have left. Andy will discuss the evolution of the technology, the current state-of-the-art, and paint a picture of where we are going.
